Title: ChatGPT becomes first AI chatbot to face tougher EU rules
Article:
BRUSSELS: ChatGPT will have to comply with tougher safety rules after the EU added it Monday to a list of digital services subject to greater legal scrutiny, a first for an AI chatbot.
Brussels also designated Reddit and Roblox as "very large" online platforms, a label that comes with additional obligations and oversight.
"ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox will now be held to a higher standard of scrutiny and accountability in the European Union, in line with their large impact on our citizens and society," EU technology chief Henna Virkkunen said.
The "very large" designation applies to platforms and search engines with more than 45 million monthly active users in the 27-nation bloc, a threshold ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox reported meeting, the commission said.
The three now have four months to comply with additional obligations under the Digital Services Act (DSA), a content law that is a major weapon in the legal armoury the EU has deployed to rein in Big Tech in recent years.
These include "assessing and mitigating the systemic risks stemming from their service and algorithmic systems related to the dissemination of illegal content, the negative effects on minors, users' physical and mental well-being, fundamental rights, electoral processes and public security," Brussels said.
To bring it under the DSA's regulatory umbrella, the commission qualified ChatGPT as a search engine.
Lena-Maria Boswald, of the German tech think tank Interface, said ahead of the announcement that the expected move would set a "precedent" and "influence the regulatory expectations for every large generative AI system used in the EU."
"OpenAI already has risk-management obligations under the AI Act, but the DSA could widen the scope," she said.
The widened scrutiny will also apply to Roblox, a gaming platform that lets people build their own games and share them with others, and Reddit, the popular online forum.
The designations come as the EU has stepped up regulatory enforcement against the world's biggest digital platforms, including many American ones, despite strong US pushback and threats of retaliation.
It recently told TikTok, one of the about 30 other listed platforms, to change what it deemed its addictive design or face heavy fines.
And last year it hit Elon Musk's social media platform X with a 120-million-euro (US$138 million) fine for breaching transparency obligations and other violations.

Title: Malaysia seeks Nepal's nod to deploy Smart team for rescue operations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has sought permission from the Nepalese government to deploy the
Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart)
to assist in search and rescue (SAR) operations following floods and landslides in the country.
The matter was conveyed by Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan during a phone conversation with his Nepalese counterpart, Shisir Khanal, on Monday.
"The discussion focused on the latest developments in the SAR operations, particularly efforts to locate Malaysians who remain uncontactable following the floods and landslides in Nepal recently," Mohamad wrote on his official Facebook page.
He also thanked the Nepalese government for the assistance and cooperation extended to the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu in dealing with the situation.
On Sunday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was reported as saying that the Madani government had decided to send the Smart team t
o Nepal to assist in SAR
operations following the floods that hit the country.
Anwar said the Smart team was also tasked with locating and bringing home affected Malaysians, as well as assisting the Malaysian Embassy in Nepal in coordinating aid and ensuring their safety and welfare.
He said Malaysia would also contribute US$1 million to Nepal to assist affected victims and support post-disaster recovery efforts.
According to the Foreign Ministry, 55 Malaysians remained uncontactable after flash floods and landslides struck on Aug 26.
Meanwhile, Anadolu Ajansi reported that the death toll from flash floods and landslides along the Nepal-China border had risen to at least 919, while nearly 4,800 people were reported missing, including 853 foreign nationals, according to authorities on Monday.
Six days after the disaster struck, SAR operations were still ongoing in the affected areas, with authorities also working to reach workers stranded at several hydroelectric projects.

Title: Muhyiddin backs cost-of-living measures, seeks broader relief in 2027 Budget
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin has welcomed the government's latest measures to ease cost-of-living pressures and support businesses, but called for broader relief under the 2027 Budget.
The Bersatu president said restoring the monthly subsidised RON95 entitlement from 200 litres to 300 litres and raising the e-Invoice exemption threshold to businesses with annual sales of up to RM3 million would ease pressure on households and businesses facing rising costs.
He also welcomed other measures announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, including an additional RM500 million for school maintenance, digitalisation of public healthcare services, free access to selected artificial intelligence software for youths, an additional RM1 billion in microcredit facilities for small traders and a RM200 million grant for hawkers, night-market traders and women running home-based businesses.
"I welcome the Prime Minister's announcement of measures to ease the people's cost-of-living burden, assist businesses and strengthen government service delivery," he said in a statement today.
Muhyiddin said the measures would improve government services in education, healthcare and the digital economy while supporting micro, small and medium enterprises.
He said the additional assistance was particularly important for businesses facing rising operating costs.
He urged ministries and government agencies to disburse the allocations promptly and ensure assistance reached all eligible individuals and businesses.
"Following the announcement of these measures, it is important for the relevant ministries and government agencies to channel the allocations immediately and ensure that every form of assistance reaches those eligible," he said.
However, Muhyiddin said the measures should not be seen as a final solution to the pressures facing Malaysians and businesses.
He said they should be followed by broader measures under the 2027 Budget to ease the cost of living, support businesses and stimulate economic growth.
"This includes reviewing policies on taxation and subsidy rationalisation, which are seen to have a direct impact on the burden currently borne by the people," he said.
Anwar announced the
six measures during his National Day Eve
address at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre yesterday, saying the government had decided to act before the Budget because cost-of-living pressures and business needs could not wait until October.

Title: Spanish PM blames Russia, Israel for disinformation in Ceuta migrant crisis
Article:
MADRID: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said on Monday there were signs Russia and Israel had spread the disinformation over Spain's migration policy that triggered last month's rush of migrants into Ceuta, but no evidence of Moroccan involvement.
Over 72,000 migrants irregularly crossed from Morocco into the tiny Spanish territory between July 30 and 31 in an unprecedented surge at one of the European Union's only two land borders with Africa, prompting alarm across the bloc.
At least 100 people died in the attempt, according to Ceuta's local authorities.
Spanish opposition parties and some human rights groups have accused Rabat of deliberately allowing the mass crossing, an accusation Morocco has denied.
"When people talk and speculate about the participation of Moroccan authorities, I deny this outright," Sanchez told radio station SER.
Videos on Instagram, TikTok and other social media spread misleading claims that migrants reaching Ceuta by sea could remain in Spain, encouraging thousands to attempt the crossing, Spanish authorities have said.
Sanchez said research by the EU's diplomatic service EEAS had indicated that Russian and Israeli networks had been behind the spread of disinformation in conjunction with far-right networks.
He said it was clear that the two countries had used the crisis to criticise Madrid due to dissatisfaction with its position on the wars in Ukraine and Gaza, but gave no further details on the evidence he had of their involvement.
Israel's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Russia's Embassy in Spain and the EEAS did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.
Roughly 5,000 migrants, some seeking asylum, have remained in Ceuta since the border rush, triggering near-daily protests from locals against the Spanish government's handling of the crisis and sporadic attacks against a makeshift migrant camp at El Trampolin beach, according to police reports.
Police arrested three Moroccan citizens on Sunday for lobbing bottles filled with corrosive liquids against an army patrol in Ceuta, news agency EFE reported, citing police sources.
No one was injured in the attack, the report added.
Sanchez also announced on Monday that the cabinet would deploy an additional €168 million (US$195 million) in emergency funds to reactivate Ceuta's economy, a figure equivalent to eight per cent of the enclave's gross domestic product, on top of €180 million pledged last week for medium-term recovery efforts.

Title: Veterinary Services Department recognises 167 artificial insemination technicians nationwide
Article:
SERDANG: The Veterinary Services Department (DVS) today recognised 167 artificial insemination technicians nationwide for their commitment to strengthening livestock breeding services at the field level.
Veterinary Services director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Noor Hisham Mohd Haron said the recognition, covering the 2024 to 2026 period, included several categories, among them the Golden Hands Award for DVS and private artificial insemination technicians.
He said the assessment also took into account artificial insemination service achievements, including the number of livestock receiving the service, the number of offspring born through artificial insemination and the number of livestock successfully impregnated through the procedure.
"This award presentation is an important platform to appreciate the high commitment of artificial insemination technicians who are the frontliners in driving the genetic transformation of the country's livestock," he said in his speech at the Award and Appreciation Presentation Ceremony for Artificial Insemination Technicians and Livestock Farmers and the launch of the Artificial Insemination Management System (AIMS) here.
Held at Laman Veterinar, MAEPS Serdang, the ceremony also saw the launch of AIMS, a digital system developed by DVS to streamline the management of artificial insemination services in an integrated and real-time manner.
AIMS covers the management of premises and livestock data, frozen semen stock inventory, artificial insemination procedure records, as well as information on pregnancy examinations and livestock births.
Mohd Noor Hisham said the system would not only improve operational efficiency in the field, but also help strengthen the integrity of national data related to livestock breeding.
"More accurate and integrated data is important to support policy planning, the development of high-performance livestock breeds as well as efforts to strengthen the country's food security," he said.
The ceremony also saw the introduction of the AIMS Digital Transformation Award 2026 and the Premier Award for Reproductive Technology Application (ART) 2026, recognising efforts to promote the use of technology in the livestock breeding industry.
Agriculture and Food Security Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Isham Ishak and DVS senior management were also present.

Title: Beyond Merdeka: Building strategic resilience in a volatile world
Article:
LETTER:
Malaysia has achieved remarkable development and regional influence for the past six decades. For the generation that fought for independence, Merdeka meant freedom from colonial domination.
Today, however, threats to independence come through economic dependency, energy insecurity, disrupted supply chains, technological dependence and geopolitical conflicts taking place thousands of kilometres away.
The current conflict in the Middle East, for example, affect countries far beyond the battlefield. Oil prices rise overnight. Shipping routes become insecure. Air travel disrupted.
Tourism can decline. Global markets can become volatile. Industries dependent on petroleum and petrochemicals can face increasing costs. In an interconnected world, distance no longer guarantees protection from geopolitical consequences.
Political independence alone is no longer enough. A nation must also possess economic resilience and strategic independence in every aspect of governance.
Malaysia is fortunate to have some energy resources and a strong petroleum and gas industry. Yet the Middle East conflict reminds that energy security is not enough.
Perhaps this is a time to explore more oil and gas towards being an Energy Hub with the latest research saying the world still very much depends on oil and gas at least till 2050.
Another aspect is increasing food prices due to disruption of importation of fertilisers from Middle East as well as increasing fuel prices.
Every day, Malaysia faces a growing food waste challenge with an estimated to generate approximately 17,000 tonnes of food waste daily.
What if Kuala Lumpur's food waste could be transformed into valuable organic fertiliser by emulating the experiences of Korea, Germany and France.
Estimates suggest that if all food waste generated in Kuala Lumpur were systematically collected and converted into high-quality organic compost, it could potentially support the nutrient and soil-structural needs of over 8,000 hectrares  of agricultural land every year.
Several countries have already demonstrated that food waste can become a valuable resource.
In South Korea and Germany, food and organic waste are collected separately and processed, producing organic fertiliser and renewable energy.
The Middle East conflict also provides an important warning for the tourism industry.
Wars and geopolitical crises can immediately affect tourism through rising airfares, airspace closures, travel warnings and declining international confidence.
Malaysia's tourism strategy must therefore focused on being resilient. Asean, East Asia, South Asia, Central Asia, West Asia and Europe should all remain important components of Malaysia's tourism strategy.
Perhaps the most important lesson from the conflicts of our time concerns foreign policy. In an increasingly divided world, countries are often pressured to choose sides.
Great-power competition, regional rivalries and ideological conflicts can place smaller and medium-sized countries in difficult positions.
This does not mean remaining silent in the face of injustice.
Malaysia should continue to support peace, international law, humanitarian principles and dialogue but also avoid becoming unnecessarily involved in any conflicts that do not serve its national interests.
Such a foreign policy, which Malaysia has practised continuously, will surely benefit Malaysians for generations to come.
DR MEHDI SOLTANZADEH
Senior Lecturer
Academy of Malay Studies
Universiti Malaya

Title: BN strategy for Melaka polls must reflect grassroots wishes, component party leaders said
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two Barisan Nasional component party leaders said the coalition must make decisions that closely reflect the wishes of its grassroots in determining its strategy for the Melaka election.
MIC president Tan Sri S.A. Vigneswaran said the approach was important to ensure BN continued to lead Melaka.
"In terms of strategy, ideally we would have good negotiations with all parties, but that may not be achievable at this point.
"So we must take the path closest to the wishes of the grassroots to ensure BN can continue to lead the state," he told reporters.
He was responding to comments by Universiti Utara Malaysia political analyst Prof Dr Mohd Azizuddin Mohd Sani, who said BN would have an advantage if it contested the election alone, as it could retain the status quo in its 21 seats without needing an alliance.
Vigneswaran said BN's supreme council would meet soon to discuss the proposals, with all component parties given an opportunity to put forward their views before the coalition agreed on the best course of action.
"All BN component parties are given room to put forward proposals, and after that we will take the best views," he said.
On MIC's seat allocation, Vigneswaran said the party would contest one state seat in the Melaka election, the same seat it defended in 2021, when its candidate VP Shanmugam won the Gadek seat with a 559-vote majority in a six-cornered contest.
"If we want to ask for more, it must be reasonable. We can ask, but we must understand that the most important thing is for BN to lead the state.
"If we ask for more as we please and end up not winning, then there is no point," he said.
Vigneswaran also said the position of MIC deputy president Datuk Seri M. Saravanan within the party remained unchanged despite the former human resources minister currently facing court charges.
Meanwhile, MCA secretary-general Datuk Chong Sin Woon said all strategic proposals for BN in the Melaka election, including contesting alone, could be considered, with one exception.
"MCA's position is clear. Not with DAP. That is the decision of last year's MCA General Assembly resolution.
"Other than that, all proposals can be considered," he said.

Title: Tighter controls, stronger finances behind Budi Madani fuel quota restoration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Improved supply management, stricter enforcement and the government's sound fiscal position were key factors in the restoration of Budi Madani fuel quotas from 200 to 300 litres.
The Finance Ministry said the reinstatement of the monthly quota would take effect automatically for Budi Madani Ron95 (Budi95) and Budi Madani Diesel from tomorrow.
The ministry said the decision also took into account the needs of Malaysians who travel long distances for daily necessities and small traders who depend on vehicles for their livelihoods.
The adjustment covers 16 million consumers currently enjoying Ron95 at the subsidised price of RM1.99 per litre, of whom more than 700,000 are also eligible for subsidised diesel at RM2.10 per litre.
Eligible owners of private diesel pickup trucks and four-wheel-drive vehicles may apply for an additional 100 litres per month, bringing their total monthly entitlement to 400 litres.
Those who have already been approved for the additional 100 litres will have their entitlement automatically adjusted to 400 litres from Sept 1, while those who have not yet applied may do so through the Budi Madani portal.
The ministry said the government would continue to ensure fuel subsidies were channelled to eligible Malaysians, while strengthening efforts to curb leakage, smuggling and misuse.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim
announced the restoration of the quota,
a move that was among six immediate measures introduced to ease cost-of-living pressures and support Malaysians ahead of the 2027 Budget tabling in October.
On March 26, Anwar announced a temporary reduction, effective April 1, in response to
surging global oil prices
driven by the ongoing Middle East conflict.
At the time of the reduction, the monthly subsidy bill for
RON95 and diesel had risen
to an estimated RM4 billion, based on Brent crude oil prices reaching US$100 per barrel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Serian, Kuching, Samarahan, Sri Aman record hazardous API readings at 5pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sarawak's air quality continued to worsen, with four monitoring stations recording hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5pm today.
Of the four, Serian recorded the highest API reading at 441, followed by Kuching at 373, Samarahan at 351 and Sri Aman at 334.
According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), four other areas in Sarawak recorded "very unhealthy" API readings, with Sarikei registering 281, Sibu 246, Mukah 216 and Samalaju 201.
Eleven areas recorded "unhealthy" readings.
They included Bintulu (181), ILP Miri (175), Miri (175), Kapit (167) and Limbang (163) in Sarawak.
Outside Sarawak, Labuan recorded an API reading of 165, while three areas in Sabah also recorded "unhealthy" readings. They were Kota Kinabalu at 153, Kimanis at 142 and Tawau at 134.
Sungai Petani in Kedah and Seberang Jaya in Penang also recorded "unhealthy" API readings at 154 and 152 respectively.
An API reading of between zero and 50 is categorised as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and above 300 as hazardous.

Title: South Korea court gives Unification Church leader two years in prison
Article:
SEOUL: A South Korean court sentenced the leader of the secretive and powerful Unification Church on Monday to two years in prison on charges of bribing officials, including the wife of the then president.
Han Hak-ja, 83, was accused of providing luxury items, including a designer handbag, to former first lady Kim Keon Hee while her husband, Yoon Suk Yeol, was president, in an attempt to secure policy favours.
She arrived Monday for sentencing – at which prosecutors had sought a 13-year term – in a wheelchair, wearing hospital pyjamas and a surgical mask, surrounded by aides.
The Unification Church has a range of significant business interests, including media, education and food distribution, and has long drawn scrutiny over its political ties in South Korea.
In a statement to AFP, the church vowed to appeal, saying it disagreed with the court's ruling.
"We cannot accept the court's finding today that Han instructed the acts in question or was aware of and approved their unlawful purpose," it said Monday.
Other allegations against Han include providing illegal funds to once-prominent former lawmaker Kweon Seon-dong, who is now in prison for receiving bribes.
"We have confirmed that she has been sentenced to two years" by the Seoul Central District Court, a spokesman for the Unification Church told AFP.
"Given that she stands at the apex of the Unification Church, and considering her position and role... a prison sentence is unavoidable," the court said in its ruling, Yonhap news agency reported.
Suspension
Founded in 1954 by Han's late husband, Moon Sun-myung, the Unification Church has long drawn controversy over teachings that regard Moon as the Second Coming of Jesus Christ.
Han, revered by church members as the "True Mother", took the helm of the church after Moon's death in 2012. She was arrested in September 2025 in connection with a bribery case involving the former first lady.
The Unification Church is best known for its mass wedding ceremonies, in which couples of different nationalities are matched, held at its headquarters in South Korea.
Han's arrest rocked the church, which claims to have 10 million followers worldwide.
Since her arrest, Han has repeatedly been transferred between a detention centre and hospital for medical treatment.
After the verdict, the church leader returned to hospital, where the court ruled she could remain until Wednesday due to medical issues including a heart condition, pain from a fall and glaucoma treatment.
"Whether she will seek a further suspension remains a matter for discussion among her attorneys in consideration of her health conditions," the church spokesman told AFP.
The church came under renewed scrutiny in Japan after the 2022 assassination of former prime minister Shinzo Abe, with the suspected gunman blaming the organisation for his family's financial ruin.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: National Unity Ministry remains committed to strengthening national unity, social harmony
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government, through the National Unity Ministry, remains committed to strengthening unity and social harmony in line with the National Unity Policy.
National Unity Ministry secretary-general Datuk Haslina Abdul Hamid said this was being pursued through various programmes and initiatives aimed at strengthening social integration, fostering patriotism and building a more inclusive society.
"I believe that through a spirit of togetherness, mutual respect and a willingness to accept differences, we can ensure that the well-being enjoyed today is safeguarded for future generations.
"The legacy left by our past leaders should serve as guidance and an example in shaping the country's development.
"This will ensure that the country's development and administration can continue in an atmosphere of peace and harmony," she said when met at the 2026 Anak Merdeka Malaysia celebrations here today.
Meanwhile, she expressed hope that programmes such as the Anak Merdeka Malaysia celebrations would continue and expand in the years to come.
She said such programmes not only celebrated those born on National Day and Malaysia Day, but also provided Malaysians with an opportunity to connect with the country's history and identity.
"It would not be complete to commemorate National Day without highlighting the significant contributions of the Father of Independence, the late Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra Al-Haj.
"He was the leader who spearheaded negotiations with the British, leading to the country achieving independence on Aug 31, 1957," she said.
Haslina said Tunku Abdul Rahman's wise leadership, rooted in consultation and consensus, ensured that the voices of people from various races were heard and respected.
"This is the spirit that we must continue to embrace and pass down so that the independence we achieved remains the foundation for peace, prosperity and national unity," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia probes citizens alleged to have fought for Russia in Ukraine
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia said on Monday it was investigating claims that "several" citizens had joined the Russian military and were deployed in the war in Ukraine.
The information, which came from Ukrainian authorities, was being verified with several ministries and government institutions, the foreign ministry in Jakarta said in a statement.
It did not say how many Indonesians were under suspicion.
If the information is true, the fighters risk losing their citizenship under a law that requires Indonesians to obtain presidential permission if they want to serve a foreign military.
"If the involvement of Indonesian citizens in the armed forces of a foreign country is verified, it is an individual act and does not represent the policy or position of the Indonesian government," the ministry said.
Indonesia has not traditionally been a source of mercenaries for Russia or Ukraine, which have both recruited foreign fighters throughout the war.
"Information regarding the identity, citizenship status, recruitment process, and form of involvement of the individuals mentioned still needs to be further confirmed," the foreign ministry said.
"The Indonesian government will also investigate the possibility of fraud, exploitation, or recruitment through job offers that are not in accordance with the intended purpose."
Citizens from African countries have reportedly been forcibly conscripted into the Russian army to fight in Ukraine after being lured with promises of jobs abroad.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Born on National Day, Malaysia Day: A birthday like no other
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: For some Malaysian families, Aug 31 and Sept 16 are more than dates on the national calendar - they are birthdays, too.
For Fasha Erma Mohd Khomari, 34, both dates have a place on her family calendar.
Her 10-year-old son, Muhammad Zulfaqar Sharif, was born on Aug 31, 2016, while his 12-year-old brother, Muhammad Nail Sharif, arrived on Sept 16, 2014.
The mother of five said she felt blessed that her sons shared their birthdays with two of the country's most significant celebrations in Malaysia.
"I feel grateful because these are special days and whenever they are celebrated, everyone will remember their birthdays too.
"It feels like people appreciate their birthdays, so I feel very happy about it," she said when met at the 2026 Anak Merdeka Malaysia celebrations today.
Asked how they felt about sharing their birthdays with the country's celebrations, the boys said they were happy.
"We are very happy to celebrate our birthdays with fireworks every year," they said.
However, when they were younger, Fasha Erma said the boys did not quite understand why their birthdays always fell during a school holiday.
"When they were in Year One, they would ask why their birthdays were never celebrated with their friends.
"We told them that their birthdays fell on a public holiday, so if they wanted to celebrate with their friends, we had to do it earlier.
"When they reached Year Two or Three, they began to understand and would say, 'Oh, it is because of Merdeka and Malaysia Day'," she said.
For Nik Fatihah Nik Mat Yusoff, 40, Sept 16 is also a date etched into her family's story.
Her son, Anas Muadz, now 10, was born on Malaysia Day in 2016, two weeks earlier than his expected due date.
Fatihah said she never expected her child to arrive on Sept 16 but came to see it as a blessing.
"I felt lucky because it was Sept 16. I did not expect my child to be born on that day.
"When I realised it was Malaysia Day, I felt happy because the child gets a public holiday and the birthday coincides with Malaysia Day," she said.
For Jennifer Ang, 42, Aug 31 is the day she remembers as both a National Day celebration and the unexpected arrival of her son, Jayden Koh.
Jayden, who turned 13 this year, was due on Sept 11 but decided to arrive early, on the eve of National Day.
"Actually, his due date was Sept 11, 2013. It is quite a nice number, 9-1-1, but he suddenly decided he wanted to pop out.
"It is a very special day for us as Malaysians. When he was born that night, I could see the fireworks from the hospital window," she said.
For Jayden, growing up with a National Day birthday has given the date an added sense of pride.
"I felt proud and happy when I realised that I was born on Aug 31," he said.
For Yasmine Hasan, 41, her daughter Arfa Zety Umairah Anwar's Aug 31 birthday has also become a reason for the family to make the most of National Day celebrations.
Arfa, who was born in 2017 following an emergency caesarean section due to complications, celebrated her birthday this year by joining other National Day babies at the programme.
"I am very happy to celebrate my birthday with my friends at this event today," Arfa said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tunku Azizah Hospital welcomes 12 Merdeka babies
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: As the nation celebrated its 69th National Day, 12 newborns, including a pair of twin girls, began their life stories at the Tunku Azizah Hospital (HTA) today.
All ten 'Merdeka babies' were delivered between midnight and noon, comprising six baby boys and six baby girls.
HTA director Dr Shamsul Anuar Kamarudin said a birth on National Day is not only a special date, but it also carries a deeper meaning as a symbol of life, hope and the nation's future.
"Every birth is not just a number. It represents a family, a hope and a trust for the future," he said in his speech at the HTA 2026 Merdeka Baby celebration.
For Nor Asyikin Mat Zain, 29, the birth of her second child on National Day made the occasion even more meaningful, especially since both her children were born on dates of great significance.
She said her firstborn, now four years old, was born on Jan 1, while her second child, a baby boy weighing 3.13kg, arrived naturally at 5.45am today.
"Honestly, I'm so proud. My first was born on New Year's Day, and now her little brother arrives on National Day," she told Bernama.
Meanwhile, Siti Zulaikha Mohd Jasni, 33, became the first mother to deliver a Merdeka baby at HTA this year, when her baby boy, weighing 2.78kg, was born via caesarean section at 12.05am.
Although he arrived earlier than his expected due date of Sept 8, she said the birth has made Aug 31 an even more meaningful date for her family.
For Rajeah Amud, 32, the arrival of her first child on National Day was nothing short of a blessing. Her baby girl was delivered naturally at 7.55am, despite being due on Sept 8.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Serpent' Netanyahu tricks US into war: Iran FM
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Monday called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a "serpent", accusing him of tricking Washington into going to war with the Islamic republic.
"In Hebrew, Netanyahu openly crows that he suckered the US Administration into a war on Iran on behalf of Israel.
"Netanyahu explicitly laughs about how he 'influenced' America through 1,000 hours of airtime on US networks," Araghchi said in a post on X.
"In English, he praises POTUS' leadership. Serpent," he added.
War broke out between Iran and the United States on Feb 28 with US-Israeli strikes killing the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ali Khamenei along with senior military officials.
Iran retaliated with attacks across the region as the conflict continued to spread.
An April ceasefire put an end to the most intense fighting, but sporadic attacks mainly near the Strait of Hormuz have dimmed prospects for a final peace agreement, and the US recently shifted toward a campaign of what it calls "economic asphyxiation" of Iran.
The US struck the Iranian island of Larak late Sunday, its first such attack in a month.
In response, Iran says it launched attacks on bases in Jordan and the UAE used by the US military.
Last week, Netanyahu dismissed any prospect of an Iran-US deal and called Iran's leaders "savages."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AEON Bank rolls out Merdeka Bonus campaign to drive digital payments
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: AEON Bank Malaysia has rolled out its Merdeka Bonus campaign in conjunction with Merdeka and Malaysia Day 2026, offering rewards to customers while encouraging wider adoption of digital payments.
The digital bank said the six-week campaign was designed to reward customers while encouraging more consumers to embrace the convenience of digital payments for their daily transactions.
"The campaign also reflects the bank's commitment to fostering continuous progress across the fintech industry, creating opportunities and value-added benefits in everyday life, and enabling local businesses to participate and grow in an omnichannel digital economy," it said in a statement.
As part of the campaign, AEON Bank held an on-ground activation at Pasar Seni on Aug 21, attracting members of the public to participate in its Merdeka and Malaysia Day activities.
A total of 30 winners from various backgrounds took home the exclusive AEON Bank Neko Plushie: Malaysian Food Edition.
AEON Bank said this year's campaign also reflected its commitment to making digital banking more engaging and intuitive for Malaysians, particularly students, working professionals and the wider community.
By leveraging its cloud-native agility and artificial intelligence (AI) optimisation, combined with its Shariah-compliant financing capabilities, the bank aims to provide secure, seamless and Shariah-compliant banking solutions.
"The bank is committed to empowering the community in pursuing its financial aspirations and achieving economic independence, while cultivating a more inclusive financial future for all.
"We will continue to contribute towards positioning Malaysia as an Islamic banking hub in the region and fostering the growth of the nation's digital economy," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Israel signs three-billion-euro arms export deal with Greece
Article:
JERUSALEM: Israel's Defence Ministry announced Monday it had signed a deal with Athens worth approximately three billion euros to set up an "Achilles Shield" aerial defence system for Greece.
"Under the deal, Israel will build Greece a comprehensive, multi-layered air defence array, drawing entirely on Israeli-made systems and on the extensive operational experience Israel's defence establishment has gained during the war," the ministry said in a statement.
It added that "this is the largest defence export deal in the history of Israel-Greece relations, and one of the largest in the history of the State of Israel".
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Over 4,800 foreigners inspected in 334 ops in Terengganu
Article:
DUNGUN: The Terengganu Immigration Department inspected 4,884 foreigners through 334 operations across the state from January to Aug 15.
Its director, Mohd Yusri Mohd Nor, stated that out of that number, 1,257 illegal immigrants were detained for various immigration offences.
He said most of the illegal immigrants were detained in a joint operation with the cooperation of agencies such as the National Security Council (NSC), local authorities and police.
"This operation targeted high-risk areas such as construction sites, residential homes employing foreign workers, business premises, plantation areas and housing," he said in a statement today.
Yusri said that out of the total arrests, 522 undocumented migrants were detained for offences under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, which is for not possessing valid documents or permits.
He said that 317 more were detained for overstaying under Section 15(4) of the Immigration Act 1959/6, while 372 people were detained for misuse of passes under Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations.
Meanwhile, he said that 46 more people were detected committing various other offences.
He said the Terengganu Immigration also opened 207 investigation papers related to immigration offences during that period, while RM2.887 million in fines were collected.
"A total of 727 people have been charged in court, consisting of 707 illegal immigrants and 20 employers who hired or sheltered illegal immigrants. From the cases brought to court, a total of RM602,000 in fines have been recorded so far," he said.
He said that during that period, a total of 2,376 detainees were deported from the country this year.
Meanwhile, Yusri said that Immigration deputy director-general Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli also participated in the integrated operation to hunt for illegal immigrants in the Bukit Besi near here on Aug 11.
In that operation, it was reported that 99 foreigners were inspected and 49 PATI were detained for offences under the Immigration Act 1959/63 and the Immigration Regulations 1963.
"Of the total number of illegal immigrants detained, 24 were Bangladeshis, 17 Indonesians, seven Myanmar nationals and one Indian national," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Oil palm entrepreneur loses nearly RM250,000 to bogus investment scheme on TikTok
Article:
TANGKAK: A 56-year-old oil palm entrepreneur's hopes of making high returns within a short period were dashed after she lost nearly RM250,000 to a bogus investment syndicate.
The woman fell victim to the scam after coming across an investment advertisement on social media on May 6.
District police chief Superintendent Roslan Mohd Talib said the suspect lured the victim by offering high returns if she joined the investment scheme.
"The victim was interested and joined the scheme on TikTok before making 18 separate transactions totalling RM245,403 into three accounts provided by the suspect.
"The transactions were made from July 1 to Aug 22.
"The victim only realised she had been duped after she failed to receive the promised returns," he said in a statement.
Roslan said the victim subsequently lodged a report at the Tangkak district police headquarters.
He said the case is being investigated under  Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: In London, son's agonising wait for news of parents missing in Nepal-Tibet floods
Article:
SINCE a catastrophic flood struck the border area between Nepal and Tibet, Prajval Haldia in London has had no word from his parents who were on a pilgrimage in the region at the time.
The 22-year-old's parents, Kavitha and Pavan Haldia, were part of a group of 16 members of a Hindu temple in south London who were on an organised trip when the tsunami-like disaster happened on Wednesday.
"We get a call every day from a foreign office, but they don't really have any news," Haldia told AFP on Saturday.
The group belong to the Sanatan Mandir and Community Centre in Coulsdon.
A priest, Nabhi Nandan Das, was among the pilgrims, who were due to visit the sacred Hindu site of Mount Kailash, according to a spokesperson for the temple.
Haldia learned of the floods from media reports around midday on Wednesday and immediately tried to call his parents.
"Obviously the ringing tone didn't even come up. It was just straight to voicemail", he recalled.
Haldia described checking where his parents were located.
"Slowly, obviously the picture came together that they were supposed to be in the same area where like exactly where it hit," he described.
"We know that they had left for the border crossing at Gyirong in the morning, and there's been no contact from them since they reached at least the Nepalese side of the border crossing, and they're on their way into China or Tibet"," Haldia explained.
Four days after the disaster, the young man still has "no news at all."
According to the Nepal Tourism Board, 33 British nationals are among the hundreds of foreigners reported missing.
"Obviously, I understand it's hard to get information out of that area because of obviously the destruction ... (and) all the people are focused on the rescue.
"It's just been very difficult", he added, still in shock.
Haldia has been speaking to the relatives of other people missing from the same group.
"Obviously it's quite hard, but the whole community has been incredibly supportive."
"It's just I guess trying to stay positive, everyone together," he said.
Unlike other relatives of the missing, Prajval does not plan to travel to the region at this stage, preferring to "stay contactable."
"I'm the only child, the only next of kin really in the family," Haldia told AFP.
"Spending hours on a plane at the moment in the situation, I don't think is the (right) move because it's so early on."
He also worries about feeling useless on the ground and even making the rescue effort "more problematic."
"I'm not a rescuer. I can't really contribute to that effort in any way.
"I think the focus should obviously be on rescuing as many people as possible from this disaster", he added, hoping that his parents will be found safe and sound.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Maha draws over a million visitors, nearly RM6mil in sales
Article:
SERDANG: More than one million people have visited the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (Maha) 2026 in its first three days, generating nearly RM6 million in sales.
Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the massive turnout also saw about 184,000 vehicles enter and leave the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang (Maeps).
"Traffic has been very heavy around the Maha grounds," he told reporters after launching Laman Padi.
Mohamad, commonly known as Mat Sabu, said sales were expected to pick up towards the end of the exhibition, when visitors typically make larger purchases, particularly of plant seeds.
"Regarding sales, we will see how it goes because visitors tend to spend more towards the end of Maha, especially on purchases of plant seeds," he said.
The heavy visitor flow has led to congestion around the site, prompting organisers to add shuttle services to address complaints about traffic and long queues.
Mohamad said the organising committee meets nightly to resolve operational issues, including long queues at the state pavilions.
"I saw very long queues in front of the state pavilions earlier. We have told the management to find ways to transport visitors more quickly, especially in the hot weather," he said.
Maha 2026, which runs until Sept 6, aims to attract four million visitors and record RM58 million in direct sales.
Earlier, Mohamad said 121 memorandums of understanding involving
potential investments
worth RM8 billion are expected to be signed during the 10-day event.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Car bomb in front of Mexico police station wounds seven
Article:
ZACATECAS: A car bomb exploded in front of a police station in Mexico overnight Sunday, wounding seven people, authorities said.
The blast happened in Ojocaliente in the state of Zacatecas, where Mexico's two largest drug cartels are fighting for control of key drug-trafficking routes.
It was the third explosive attack in Zacatecas in less than a week, according to an AFP tally.
"The explosive was placed in a private vehicle and caused physical damage to the station and properties located nearby," state government secretary Rodrigo Reyes said on Facebook.
Six civilians were reported wounded, Reyes said in an earlier post, adding that they were receiving medical care.
One police officer was also wounded in the blast, which damaged 13 vehicles, including two police patrol cars, he said.
Local authorities said school classes would be suspended on Monday and celebrations for the town's patron saint festival were cancelled.
Zacatecas is key to the drug trade because it links central Mexico with the north and west of the country and features routes that are key to smuggling cocaine and other narcotics to the United States.
Horrific drug violence plagued the state for years, with bodies turning up and people going missing almost on a daily basis until relative calm set in.
But in July, five bodies appeared hanging from a bridge in the town of Pozos de Gamboa, about 75 kilometres (47 miles) from Ojocaliente.
The victims included a former mayor, civil servants and businesspeople from other parts of the state.
The killings drew the attention of leftist President Claudia Sheinbaum, who promised to arrest whoever was behind them.
She has deployed soldiers in violence-plagued states such as Sinaloa and Michoacan in response to threats from US President Donald Trump to intervene directly against the cartels in order to keep drugs from crossing the border into the US.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: At 101, Dr M attends National Day celebration in Putrajaya
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad attended the 2026 National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya today in an electric wheelchair.
A live video streamed on his official TikTok account, @chedetofficial, showed the 101-year-old statesman waving to the crowd.
He was also seen greeting members of the public, some of whom stopped to take photographs with him.
Dr Mahathir later shared a brief National Day message on Facebook, accompanied by a video recounting his two terms as prime minister.
"Happy Independence Day and 69th National Day, Malaysia," he said.
Dr Mahathir served as Malaysia's fourth prime minister from 1981 to 2003 and returned as the country's seventh prime minister from 2018 to 2020.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Moung Sinabung erupts, spews ash 3.5km above summit
Article:
JAKARTA: Mount Sinabung in Indonesia's North Sumatra province erupted on Monday morning, spewing a thick column of volcanic ash about 3.5 kilometres above its summit.
The Centre for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation (PVMBG) said the eruption began at 10.17 am local time with the thick, black ash column observed moving east and southeast.
"Residents and visitors or tourists are advised not to carry out activities in villages that have been relocated, as well as within a three-kilometre radius of Mount Sinabung's summit and within a 4.5-kilometre sectoral radius to the south and southeast," it said in a report published on its official website.
Mount Sinabung, located in Karo Regency, remains at Level II (Alert), while residents living near rivers originating from the volcano were advised to remain vigilant against possible volcanic mudflows.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Laman Padi enters Malaysia Book of Records with largest padi artwork
Article:
SERDANG: A 2.83ha (7acre) padi showcase at Maha 2026 has earned a place in The Malaysia Book of Records for its record-setting work of art.
Launched by Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu today, Laman Padi showcases Malaysia's padi and rice ecosystem at the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrodiversity Exhibition (Maha) 2026.
Its centrepiece is a 119ft by 126ft (36.27m by 38.4m) padi art installation, recognised by The Malaysia Book of Records as the country's largest padi art formation.
Created in collaboration with Serba Wangi Sdn Bhd, owner of the Jati rice brand, it is the first padi art installation featured at Maha.
The installation aims to highlight the potential of padi and rice to create new value through agro-tourism.
"This is not just about growing padi. We also want to encourage agro-tourism," said Mohamad.
He said the recognition showed that the padi and rice subsector could be presented creatively and innovatively beyond food production.
"This is not merely a certificate. It is recognition that Malaysian agriculture is capable of producing something unique, creative and record-setting," he said.
Laman Padi showcases the padi and rice ecosystem, from cultivation and processing to the reuse of waste generated from padi production.
It includes exhibitions, sales, cooking and padi-to-rice processing demonstrations, as well as displays on mechanisation and automation.
Maha 2026, held at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang (MAEPS), will continue until Sept 6.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Driver killed after container lorry plunges into 20m ravine
Article:
GUA MUSANG: A man was killed after the container lorry he was driving skidded and plunged into a 20-metre-deep ravine along the Gua Musang-Kuala Krai road near Ladang Serasa here today.
Gua Musang Fire and Rescue station chief Muhammad Azrul Izzham Zulkifli said the department received an emergency call at 9.11am on the incident.
He said a team of seven firefighters in three fire engines arrived at the scene at 9.58am, about 65km from the station.
"The driver was trapped in the vehicle and was pronounced dead at the scene by medical personnel.
"Firefighters extricated the victim using special equipment, with assistance from a private company's crane.
"The body of the victim was handed over to the police," he said when contacted.
He said the operation ended at 12.29pm.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal toll surges as rescuers struggle through 'unimaginable' disaster
Article:
NUWAKOT: Rescuers struggled Monday through mud and debris for a sixth day, as the number of missing people soared to nearly 5,000 since tsunami-like glacial floods roared down from the China-Nepal border, creating an "unimaginable" disaster.
The latest confirmed death toll surged above 900, but the number of those unaccounted for is also climbing – with unidentified bodies buried in mass graves after DNA sampling.
The huge wave of freezing water, rocks and debris that smashed into villages and towns on Wednesday killed at least 903 people in Nepal and in Tibet, in China, with at least 17 bodies pulled from rivers downstream in India.
Late Sunday Nepali Prime Minster Balendra Shah called the disaster "unimaginable and heartbreaking."
Rescue teams are in a race against time in treacherous conditions in a bid to free dozens of hydropower workers believed trapped in tunnels – digging, drilling and blasting through debris, a non-stop effort supported by teams from China, India and South Korea.
So far, three dead bodies have been pulled out of two tunnels, and the teams have found routes blocked with mud.
Amid the horror, there has been some hope; a six-year-old pulled out of the mud four days after the disaster on Friday was reunited with her parents after police found her crying for her mother.
"Her body was trapped in mud, but her head was outside," Nepali Armed Police spokesman Netra Bahadur Karki told AFP.
"She is out of danger and recovering at a hospital and has reunited with her family."
The disaster was sparked by a glacial collapse,  the US Geological Survey said. While the exact cause of that collapse is unclear, climate change is causing glaciers to melt worldwide, raising the risk of such disasters.
Nepali Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said: "The people of Nepal are one of the major victims of the changing climate and its impact."
Scientists say the Himalayas, the world's highest mountain range, are melting faster as global temperatures rise.
Aid needs are enormous. Entire communities have been swept away, leaving families homeless in heavy rain or sheltering in temporary facilities.
"This is an unfolding disaster," UN children's fund official Abiodun Banire told AFP, saying the needs of the tens of thousands impacted were vast.
Roads have been washed away, power plants destroyed and dozens of bridges smashed.
"We are continuing to work for search, rescue and relief operations," Karki told AFP on Monday, as communications slowly improved. Police initially had to use drones to carry messages into cut-off areas.
"Rescue teams have now reached most areas, by road or by helicopters," he added.
[[nid:1522818]]
With mortuaries overflowing with the dead, Nepal has begun burying some of the hundreds of bodies recovered after taking DNA samples so families can later retrieve them.
Kathmandu has appealed for international support, saying Nepal needed "more than a thousand" freezer units to store bodies.
Distraught families, desperate for news of missing relatives, are watching images of bodies on screens at community centres in a bid to identify the dead.
Shobha Adhikary, in the southern Nepali city of Bharatpur, told a local coordinator she believed one image showed her childhood best friend.
"It looks like him, for sure," she said, showing a photograph of a smiling, middle-aged man.
"My husband and I are best friends with Rajkumar and his wife Geeta," she said. Geeta has also been missing since Wednesday.
Among Nepal's list of the missing are 592 foreigners, including tourists who had come for trekking in its apparently serene mountains, and Hindu pilgrims seeking spiritual peace at Tibet's sacred Mount Kailash.
Nepali army rescuers said Monday its teams were working to "clear water, mud and sediment" as they dug to reach around 100 workers that the government believes may be alive inside multiple tunnels.
They are among the 933 workers at hydropower plants unaccounted for in Nepal. Workers who managed to get out described horrifying scenes when the disaster struck.
At the Upper Trishuli 3A site, rescuers broke through into the upper part of a mud-swamped tunnel, pumping air inside, then using drilling and excavator machines to dig down.
"When members of the team descended using ropes and called out to those inside, there was no response," Shah said, adding that the rescue operation was continuing.
In China, Tibet is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists, and Chinese authorities are the only source of information.
More than 2,000 personnel are part of rescue operations there, but they have faced intense challenges.
Rescuers trying to reach the epicentre of the disaster, Gyirong Port, only advanced 285 metres on Sunday, according to state media.
The glacial collapse caused the formation of huge lakes dammed by unstable debris, posing a further threat to rescue teams.
China has said 16 people died in Tibet, with 546 people missing.
In Nepal, the disaster agency raised the total number of people missing on its side of the border to 4,247, with 903 bodies recovered.
Nepal's economy is already under pressure, and foreign governments have pledged millions of dollars in humanitarian aid.
Kathmandu warns that the reconstruction bill could run into "billions of dollars."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CIA-backed investor helped top German drones firm break into US
Article:
MUNICH: German drone maker Quantum Systems gained an early foothold in the United States with help from CIA-linked investor In-Q-Tel (IQT), its co-CEO said, highlighting how US capital and networks continue to shape Europe's emerging defence companies.
Sven Kruck told Reuters that US investors including IQT helped open doors in Washington and win work with the Central Intelligence Agency and Federal Bureau of Investigation.
The comments, reported here for the first time, underscore the importance of US investors and contacts to some European defence startups even as governments across the continent push for greater independence from Washington.
"It made it easier to get started in the US with clients CIA and FBI," said Kruck, whose firm sells reconnaissance, attack and interceptor drones to countries including Ukraine and Germany.
"There were routes that opened up. That's how we found the way to the USA. We were stronger in the US early on, where the German customer was much weaker."
Berlin is seeking to reduce its dependence on Washington after President Donald Trump threatened to abandon Nato, the alliance underpinning Europe's defence against Russia.
But rebuilding Germany's long-neglected military without access to US capital and defence markets is a major challenge.
Kruck said business generated from a reconnaissance contract with US intelligence agencies was modest but helped establish Quantum's credibility. The company is now one of Europe's biggest defence startups, valued at around US$8 billion.
Like other defence companies, Quantum cannot sell technology developed in the US to other countries without US approval.
The case also underscores the growing reach of IQT, the venture capital firm established by intelligence officials to identify and invest in technologies relevant to US national security.
IQT, whose name is a nod to James Bond's gadget maker Q, owns stakes in several companies including German defence firm Stark, and is increasingly focusing on Europe as the continent ramps up military spending.
While IQT's investments are typically small, often less than US$3 million, one person with knowledge of its operations said its value lies in connecting companies with US defence buyers, the sector's top spenders.
"Europe's deep-tech ecosystem is a critical source of mission-relevant innovation," said Jennifer Nelson, executive vice president international at IQT, responding to Reuters' questions.
"Germany is a particularly important innovation partner and strategic ally," she said, calling it a "cornerstone of Europe's defence ecosystem."
The venture firm, which invests in technologies ranging from cybersecurity and energy to satellites, has backed startups including data analytics giant Palantir Technologies and Anduril, one of the biggest military technology and drone firms.
"IQT continues to expand investments in German dual-use innovators ... so allied government teams can evaluate and adopt breakthrough capabilities faster," said Nelson.
Pervasive US influence
As Europe seeks to reduce its dependence on US military power, IQT's growing presence in the region has prompted concerns that strategically important new technologies could become increasingly tied to US interests.
Marie-Agnes Strack-Zimmermann, chair of the European Parliament's security and defence committee, said IQT should be viewed differently from a conventional investor because of its links to US intelligence agencies.
"In-Q-Tel is not a purely financial investor but has a mandate to secure access to the best technologies for the US intelligence services," said Strack-Zimmermann.
"There can be strategic influence beyond the business with the United States through investment stakes, observation rights, development and licence deals as well as the access to government contracts."
Earlier this year, CIA Director John Ratcliffe said it was "optimizing our approach to working with the private sector." The CIA declined to comment.
Germany's defence ministry said it took investor influence in the defence sector seriously and that shareholders should not interfere with a company's operations, technology or research.
Kruck's comments shed light on the close links that continue to bind Europe's defence sector to the US, even as governments strive to build up domestic military capabilities.
"Every investor ... has a network behind it and, logically, you try to use this," Kruck said, adding other investors had also helped the company.
"At the end of the day, your products have to be convincing. But for sure, American investors ... know the administration that rules and make it possible to open up communication."
Kruck added, however, that IQT had not sent him a "proactive email" in the past two years.
He also pointed to Washington's requirement that foreign defence suppliers establish local operations in the US. "That is why we have factories in the US and staff there," he said.
European lawmakers have argued the region needs to do more to channel funding into startups. Europe has no equivalent of IQT.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lawyer seeks reduced sentence for Malaysian fraud victim jailed in Japan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The lawyer appointed by the family of a 24-year-old Malaysian sentenced to four years in prison in Japan will travel to the country again to attend an appeal hearing seeking a reduction of his sentence.
Lawyer Datuk Noor Svetlana Mohd Noor Nordin said the notice of appeal was filed immediately after Muhammad Faiq Zafran Mohd Jailani was sentenced, on the grounds that he was himself a victim of an online fraud syndicate.
She said the appeal would be heard on Sept 8 and handled by a legal aid lawyer at the Nagoya High Court in Kanagawa.
"Looking at the facts of the case, Faiq was offered a job as a document courier with a salary of between RM4,000 and RM6,000 a month.
"He also had no contact with any of the victims, only with two people he knew through a messaging application who gave him instructions.
"In terms of his circumstances, Faiq was not the principal offender as several others were involved, and it is clear that he was a victim of the fraud syndicate.
"Furthermore, he had only been working for 10 days and received no benefit or salary whatsoever before he was arrested by the authorities there," she told Berita Harian.
Svetlana said as Faiq was himself a victim, was still young and had only wanted to help his family financially, she was appealing to the public to contribute to a crowdfunding effort to repay the victims involved in the case.
"When Faiq was sentenced, the legal aid lawyer did not raise the matter of repayment to the victims due to the language barrier, and the four-year sentence was handed
down, which in my view should have been less than two years.
"So I am appealing to the goodwill of the public in this country to contribute whatever they can towards efforts to reduce his sentence.
"Our target is RM1 million, based on the victims' losses, but even a small amount would at least show the court that an effort is being made.
"I am not condoning what was done, but he is a victim and did not benefit in any way," she said, adding that she would travel to Japan with an assistant and Faiq's father.
She said there had been no communication with Faiq since he was sentenced, apart from confirmation during an embassy visit in July that he was in good health.
"His family does not know how he is doing due to the language barrier. The only thing the prison knows is that, as a Muslim, he cannot eat pork," she said.
It was previously
reported that Faiq was sentenced to four years' imprisonment
by the Toyama District Court on three charges, with the sentences to run concurrently from the date of his arrest on Nov 18, 2025.
Faiq was investigated in November last year under Article 246(1) of the Japanese Penal Code for fraud and Article 60 of the same code for offences committed jointly, provisions roughly equivalent to Sections 420 and 34 of the Malaysian Penal Code.
It was also previously reported that Faiq, who travelled to Japan in November last year, was believed to have fallen victim to an online scam syndicate operating in the country, which led to his detention in Toyama.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tour bus carrying 35 students crashes in Kota Belud, nine hurt
Article:
KOTA BELUD: Nine students from SM Sains Tuaran suffered minor injuries after a tour bus carrying the school group was involved in an accident at the Jalan Kota Belud-Kundasang junction today.
In the 10.55am incident, the bus was carrying 35 students and a teacher.
Kota Belud fire and rescue station chief Elge Bakuk said the department received a distress call at 11am, before a team was dispatched to the scene.
"Upon arriving at 11.40am, we found that the accident involved a tour bus carrying students from SM Sains Tuaran.
"Nine students were reported to have suffered minor injuries and were taken to Kota Belud Hospital for treatment," he said when contacted.
He said the victims were transported by ambulances from the Health Ministry in Tuaran and Kota Belud, as well as an ambulance from the Civil Defence Force.
The operation was concluded at 12.32pm, he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia seeks Nepal’s nod to deploy SMART team for flood SAR mission, says Tok Mat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Malaysia has sought permission from the Nepalese government to deploy the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) to assist in search and rescue (SAR) operations following the floods in the country.
The matter was conveyed by Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan during a phone conversation with his Nepalese counterpart, Shisir Khanal, on Monday.
“The discussion focused on the latest developments in the SAR operations, particularly efforts to locate Malaysians who remain uncontactable following the floods and landslides in Nepal recently,” Mohamad wrote on his official Facebook page.
He also expressed his appreciation to the Nepalese government for all the assistance and cooperation extended to the Embassy of Malaysia in Kathmandu in dealing with the situation.
On Sunday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was reported as saying that the Madani Government has decided to send the SMART Team to Nepal to assist with SAR operations following the flood disaster that hit the country.
Anwar said the SMART team was also tasked with locating and bringing home affected Malaysians, as well as assisting the Embassy of Malaysia in Nepal in coordinating aid and ensuring their safety and welfare.
He said Malaysia will also channel a contribution of US$1 million (RM4.02 million) to Nepal to assist affected victims and support post-disaster recovery efforts.
According to the Foreign Ministry, 55 Malaysian nationals remain uncontactable after flash floods and landslides struck on August 26.
Meanwhile, Anadolu Ajansi reported that the death toll from flash floods and landslides along the Nepal-China border had risen to at least 919, while nearly 4,800 people were reported missing, including 853 foreign nationals, according to authorities on Monday.
Six days after the disaster struck, SAR operations are still ongoing in affected areas, with authorities also working to reach workers stranded at several hydroelectric projects. — Bernama

Title: MAHA 2026 attracts 1.8 million visitors, records RM6m sales in three days
Article:
SERDANG, Aug 31 — The Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (MAHA) 2026 has recorded 1.8 million visitors and nearly RM6 million in sales in its first three days, says Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.
He said 184,000 vehicles were recorded entering and leaving the exhibition grounds during the period, reflecting heavy traffic due to the large turnout.
According to him, MAHA 2026 is targeting sales of at least RM58 million, with purchases such as crop seeds expected to contribute to the total.
“Three days have passed, and visitor turnout for MAHA has reached 1.8 million, with 184,000 vehicles moving in and out. This means very heavy traffic in the area,” he told reporters after launching Laman Padi MAHA 2026 at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang (MAEPS) today.
Commenting on transport issues following the surge in visitors, Mohamad said shuttle services had been increased and further improvements would be made based on requirements.
He said the relevant committee met daily to address complaints received and identify solutions to ensure the event ran smoothly.
“Earlier, I walked past the state pavilions and saw very long queues. We have informed the management to find ways to transport visitors quickly, especially given the current hot weather,” he said.
Mohamad said the high turnout was driven by various programmes held throughout MAHA, including MAHA Merdeka yesterday, which featured fireworks and drone shows in conjunction with National Day celebrations.
MAHA 2026, taking place from August 28 to September 6 at MAEPS, features about 2,000 exhibitors, targeting over four million visitors. — Bernama

Title: Three-year-old boy injured after foot run over by tow vehicle at Terengganu National Day parade
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 31 — A three-year-old boy sustained an injury to his left foot after it was accidentally run over by a tow vehicle taking part in the 2026 National Day parade this morning.
The boy’s mother, Puteri Anis Athirah Wan Rosli, 36, from Cendering, said the incident occurred at about 9.45 am in front of Wisma Persekutuan here.
She said her son, Che Ku Muhammad Khairul Amir Che Ku Mohd Khairul Azlan, fell before being run over by the tow vehicle carrying a Fire and Rescue Department boat.
“When the boat carrier stopped several times in front of the Wisma, my seven-year-old daughter ran ahead to take photographs. My son followed her.
“When firefighters tried to move him slightly aside for his safety, he fell forward before his foot was run over by the tow vehicle,” she told reporters at the Emergency Department of Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital (HSNZ) here.
Puteri Anis Athirah said she was relieved that an X-ray showed no broken bones, although her son remained under observation at the hospital.
She also thanked the police for their prompt response and for escorting the ambulance carrying her son to HSNZ at about 10.15am.
“I do not blame any of the firefighters. They were managing the safety and movement of the assets. I know it was an accident and happened because my son was excited,” she said.
Meanwhile, Kuala Terengganu district police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor confirmed the incident, adding that the exact cause was still under investigation. — Bernama

Title: AI programme to equip 100,000 youths for changing job market, says HR minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — The AI for the People Programme, which targets 100,000 youths aged between 18 and 30, is an important step towards preparing Malaysia’s workforce for rapid changes in the employment landscape, said Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan.
He said access to artificial intelligence (AI) technology should be expanded among youth to ensure they possessed skills relevant to the needs of the current job market and were not left behind in global technologicl developments.
“The world of employment is rapidly changing. AI, automation and digitalisation are no longer matters for the future, but have become part of today’s job market.
“As such, providing 100,000 youths with access to AI technology is an important investment to equip Malaysian talent with relevant skills and ensure they are not left behind in the changing global job landscape,” he said in a statement today.
Ramanan said the initiative also complemented the Human Resources Ministry’s (Kesuma) efforts to strengthen workforce skills through programmes such as the MyMahir AI Roadshow, which provides free Ai training to more than 22,000 Malaysians with an allocation of nearly RM110 million through Talent Corporation Malaysia Berhad (TalentCorp).
“They are all part of Malaysia’s economic strength and they cannot be left out of the government’s attention and policies.
“This approach aligns with Kesuma’s efforts to develop a more inclusive labour market, enhance workforce skills and ensure that economic and technological changes create more opportunities for the people,” he said.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced six immediate initiatives for the people, encompassing fuel subsidies, school maintenance, AI, medical digitalisation, e-Invoicing and micro business financing, which will take effect on September 1.
For the AI Programme for the People, Anwar said youths who complete the prescribed modules would receive free three-month subscriptions to AI applications, including IlmuChat, Gemini Enterprise, Wonderclip and MuleRun.
Anwar said the government also agreed to restore the basic quota of Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) programme from 200 litres to 300 litres per month, while more than half a million eligible owners of diesel-powered pickup trucks and jeeps would also receive up to 400 litres of Budi Diesel per month.
Ramanan said all the initiatives reflected the government’s comprehensive approach to ensuring that the benefits of economic growth were felt by various segments of society, particularly workers.
He added that these included low- and middle-income workers, gig workers, the self-employed, small traders and hawkers, women who generate income from home, as well as youths.
“As the Human Resources Minister, the most important thing for me is how the country’s economic strength can be felt by workers in their daily lives, whether through reduced cost-of-living pressures, skills enhancement, income-generating opportunities or support for the self-employed,” he said.
He said inclusive development rooted in the spirit of independence means that the country’s progress leaves no one behind and that the fruits of economic growth can be returned to the people.
“I am confident that under the leadership of the Prime Minister and with the cooperation of the entire government machinery, we can build a more productive, highly-skilled and prosperous Malaysia, with every worker given the opportunity to benefit from the country’s progress,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Armizan: Political maturity key to keeping unity govt stable
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Political maturity and the awareness of balancing political rights with the responsibility of nation-building are important to ensure the stability of the Unity Government, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.
In a Facebook post in conjunction with National Day today, he said the new political landscape of the country after the 15th General Election (GE15) needs to be accepted with the awareness that government stability is crucial in steering the direction of national development and the welfare of the people.
Armizan said that the political maturity demonstrated by the leadership in the Cabinet is built on awareness and unity to form a consensus of solidarity, thereby ensuring that the country has a government capable of steering the direction of development and the welfare of the people.
“I am amazed that even though the party activists have been ‘exchanging barbs’ with each other for the past few months, the relationship and interaction between the main leaders in every Cabinet Meeting has remained harmonious, constructive and professional,” he said.
He said the country’s new political landscape after the end of one-party dominance must be accepted by taking lessons from the experience between 2018 and 2022 which saw the change of three prime ministers and three Cabinet line-ups in one term.
“The change of three prime ministers and three Cabinet line-ups in one term are not a good formula for building sustainable prosperity for Malaysia,” he said.
Armizan said that political maturity and leadership within the Cabinet must be based on the awareness that the political rights of individuals and parties should be balanced with the responsibility to build the nation.
“This is the value and meaning of political maturity that is important to guide stability in the dynamics of Malaysia’s democratic and political landscape today and in the future,” he said.
In the same post, he also said that the National Month celebration is a platform for the people to express their unity in appreciating the blessings of independence and peace, while also translating it into a commitment to build the country’s future together.
“Every citizen, including leaders, civil servants, the business community, civil society activists and the general public, has their own role in the system of governance. Regardless of similarities or differences, this homeland belongs to every citizen,” he added. — Bernama

Title: King Charles conveys National Day message to Sultan Ibrahim, praises partnership and shared Commonwealth values
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — King Charles III and Queen Camilla have conveyed their congratulations to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and the people of Malaysia on the country’s National Day on Monday.
In the message shared by the British High Commission in Malaysia, King Charles expressed confidence that the UK-Malaysia Strategic Partnership would provide a valuable opportunity to deepen cooperation between the two countries in trade, technology and other shared priorities ahead of the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations in 2027.
“In particular, I hope that our two nations will continue to champion the transition to clean energy and the protection of nature and biodiversity, including through our joint leadership of the international Forest, Agriculture and Commodity Trade Dialogue.
“In this regard, I very much hope that the dialogue continues to foster cooperation and action on the ground, helping to advance sustainable commodity supply chains and strengthen the livelihoods and resilience of farming communities,” he said in the message to Sultan Ibrahim.
He noted that the contribution of smallholder farmers to food security is critically important across the Commonwealth.
Meanwhile, King Charles also reflected upon the enduring partnership between the two nations, rooted in the shared values and mutual respect that define the Commonwealth.
“I remain deeply proud of the role our family of nations plays in fostering understanding, cooperation and opportunity across the globe,” he said, adding that the longstanding educational ties between Malaysia and the United Kingdom exemplify this spirit of partnership by connecting people and empowering future generations.
King Charles said the Commonwealth’s collective strength and unity were more vital than ever in these times of global uncertainty.
“I look forward to the opportunity for our nations to come together at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in November, where we may reaffirm our shared commitments and chart a course for the future,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Sabah CM Hajiji announces RM3,000 aid for each household hit by Kota Kinabalu fire
Article:
