KOTA KINABALU, Aug 31 — The Sabah government will channel RM3,000 in aid to each Malaysian head of household (KIR) affected by a fire in Kampung Lok Buta, Numbak, here, which destroyed more than 200 homes early yesterday morning.
Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said the amount comprised RM1,000 contributions each from the state government, the federal government and the Yayasan Kebajikan Sabah.
“Alhamdulillah, I was able to visit and meet the victims of the fire. I would like to announce RM3,000 in aid for each affected head of household to help ease their burden,” he told reporters after visiting the victims at the Likas Multipurpose Hall temporary relief centre (PPS) here today.
He said the state government would also assist efforts to rebuild the victims’ homes through coordination between the State Secretary’s Office and Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA).
He said the location for rebuilding the homes, whether at the original site or elsewhere, would be determined after taking into consideration the suitability of the area.
Hajiji said that on humanitarian grounds, each non-Malaysian KIR affected by the fire in the village would also receive RM1,000 in aid from the state government.
The government will also provide basic necessities, including food and household items, to the affected families.
The fire, which broke out at about 1.40am yesterday, also claimed the lives of three children, including two siblings.
The victims were Nana Abdullah, four, her brother Mohd Asrul, six, and their eight-year-old cousin Nurfarahdilah Mohd Tajihah. — Bernama

Title: Family prays for Gelugor hiker missing in Nepal floods, Penang government ready to assist
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 31 — The family of Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad Noor Hadi, who has reportedly remained unreachable following flash floods and landslides in the Nepal-Tibet border area in Nepal last Wednesday, hopes that the hiker will be found safe.
His father, who wished to be known as Noor Hadi, said the family was now waiting for the latest updates from the authorities after being informed about the situation in Nepal and other developments.
He said the family, who live in Taman Tun Sardon, Gelugor, here, were currently in Kuala Lumpur to follow developments concerning Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad, who works with the Implementation Coordination Unit of the Prime Minister’s Department (ICU JPM) Penang, through Wisma Putra.
“Yesterday, family members attended a meeting with Wisma Putra to obtain information about Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad, and until now, we have also not received any phone calls or messages from him in Nepal.
“We hope that he will be found safe. We are constantly praying for his safety, and together with the mosque, we have also held a special prayer and recitation of Surah Yasin for him,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
Abdul Hadi said his son left for Nepal last week with two friends to undertake a hiking expedition in Langtang Valley and was scheduled to return to Malaysia today.
Meanwhile, Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the Penang government was prepared to consider appropriate forms of assistance for the families of two hikers from the state who were reported missing while hiking in Langtang Valley, Nepal, last Wednesday.
He said the state government would also obtain relevant information, including contacting the Penang Implementation Coordination Unit of the Prime Minister’s Department (ICU JPM), where the two hikers work as engineers and see how they can help.
Chow said this after the state-level National Day celebration at Padang Kota Lama here today.
Yesterday, family members and friends of the three Malaysian hikers reported missing following flash floods and landslides in the Nepal-Tibet border area last Wednesday continued to hope that they would be found safe.
Two of the climbers are Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad, 27, from Gelugor, and Muhammad Zaki Othman, 29, reportedly from Kubang Semang, Bukit Mertajam, while Muhammad Adib Haikal Awang Mansor, 27, is from Kulim, Kedah.
In a post on the Threads application, a friend of the three hikers appealed to the public to continue praying for their safety.
According to the post by user emyliatahar, the group’s last message was received at 10.42am (Malaysian time) on Aug 26, the day of the incident, with their last known location around the Bhote Koshi area. — Bernama

Title: Nine students injured after school bus carrying 36 crashes in Sabah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Nine students from Sekolah Menengah (SM) Sains Sabah suffered minor injuries after a bus carrying 35 students and a teacher was involved in an accident on the Kota Belud-Kundasang road in Sabah this morning.
According to
Utusan Malaysia
, the crash happened at about 11am at the Simpang Tiga junction.
Kota Belud Fire and Rescue Station chief Elge Bakuk said firefighters were dispatched to the scene after receiving an emergency call.
He said two personnel and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) vehicle were sent to the site, about 39km from the station.
“All the victims were later taken to Kota Belud Hospital for further treatment using ambulances from the Health Ministry in Tuaran and Kota Belud, as well as an ambulance from the Malaysian Civil Defence Force,” he said.
Elge said firefighters carried out checks at the scene to ensure the area was safe before ending the operation at 12.32pm.
No fatalities were reported, while the cause of the accident remains under investigation.

Title: From midnight to noon, Hospital Tunku Azizah welcomes 12 Merdeka babies including twin girls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — As the nation celebrated its 69th National Day, 12 newborns, including a pair of twin girls, began their life stories at Hospital Tunku Azizah (HTA) here today.
All ten ‘Merdeka babies’ were delivered between midnight and noon, comprising six baby boys and six baby girls.
HTA director Dr Shamsul Anuar Kamarudin said a birth on National Day is not only a special date, but it also carries a deeper meaning as a symbol of life, hope and the nation’s future.
“Every birth is not just a number. It represents a family, a hope and a trust for the future,” he said in his speech at the HTA 2026 Merdeka Baby celebration.
For Nor Asyikin Mat Zain, 29, the birth of her second child on National Day made the occasion even more meaningful, especially since both her children were born on dates of great significance.
She said her firstborn, now four years old, was born on Jan 1, while her second child, a baby boy weighing 3.13 kilogrammes, arrived naturally at 5.45am today.
“Honestly, I’m so proud. My first was born on New Year’s Day, and now her little brother arrives on National Day,” she told Bernama.
Meanwhile, Siti Zulaikha Mohd Jasni, 33, became the first mother to deliver a Merdeka baby at HTA this year, when her baby boy, weighing 2.78 kilogrammes, was born via caesarean section at 12.05am.
Although he arrived earlier than his expected due date of Sept 8, she said the birth has made Aug 31 an even more meaningful date for her family.
For Rajeah Amud, 32, the arrival of her first child on National Day was nothing short of a blessing. Her baby girl was delivered naturally at 7.55am, despite being due on Sept 8. — Bernama

Title: Customs sniffer dogs Goku and Cafrey join military K9s marching at Putrajaya National Day
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — While their daily routine involves tracking drugs at national entry points or performing military guard duty, K9 dogs Goku and Troy share a common mission today, namely marching alongside 33 other dogs at the National Day parade in Dataran Putrajaya.
The Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM) features 10 Labrador Retrievers — up from eight last year — led by Goku, a nine-year-old veteran dog from the Netherlands that has helped detect about 620 kilogrammes of amphetamines.
Senior Customs officer and JKDM narcotics K9 trainer Johnson Pedro Anak Ateg, 40, said first-time parade participants Cafrey and Riko were also featured after missing last year’s event due to compatibility issues with other dogs.
He said all Customs K9 dogs underwent two weeks of intensive training, matching processes, and special health screenings at Universiti Putra Malaysia’s (UPM) Veterinary Hospital.
“JKDM sniffer dogs are specifically trained to detect drugs, including methamphetamine, amphetamines, ketamine, cocaine, heroin, ecstasy, cannabis, and precursor chemicals,” he told Bernama, adding that JKDM’s drug detection dogs had recorded 41 cases up to August this year.
Johnson Pedro said that initial training for the parade involved walking the dogs individually before pairing them with compatible dogs to march side by side.
“We also provided early public exposure for the dogs through school demonstrations and walks in public areas.
“The biggest challenge is getting the dogs to walk together in unison, as some are incompatible and act aggressively towards other dogs,” he said.
Malaysia Prison Department K9 unit steps out in sunglasses and shoes during National Day parade at Dataran Putrajaya, August 31, 2026. — Bernama pic
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Armed Forces (ATM) features 25 dogs from the Army Combat Training Centre’s (Pulada) Wolf Wing, comprising guard, search, and tracking dogs, with K9 Troy out front alongside Detachment Commander Capt Duin Anak Tat.
Duin said most of the military K9s had participated in the National Day parade two or three times previously, adding that every member of the Wolf Wing was trained to handle all dogs in the unit.
“When I lead Troy, he automatically becomes the detachment leader. He is very strong; when I pull, he pulls even harder,” he said.
Duin noted that march uniformity and dog compatibility remained key challenges, as some dogs tended to pull, follow, or react if they perceived a threat, prompting veterinary officers to closely monitor their stamina and health.
To handle current weather conditions, he said all K9s were provided with ample water and vitamins, while undergoing body temperature, stool, and urine checks before deployment.
He also reminded parade visitors to seek permission from handlers before touching or taking selfies with the military dogs.
“Military dogs are highly trained. Although they appear well-behaved, an attack could happen if they perceive a threat, which is why precaution is necessary.
“Before getting closer, ask the handler first, as only the handler knows the dog’s behaviour and whether it is calm or anxious,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Suspect arrested after teen shot when hunting companion mistakes him for animal in Sarawak
Article:
MIRI, Aug 31 — The shooting case involving a 17-year-old teenager in Long Lidong, Lawas, has been resolved with the arrest of a suspect on August 25, said Lawas district police chief DSP Liong Tindan.
Liong said following the arrest of the suspect, the police also recovered a homemade firearm, locally known as a ‘
bakakuk
’, believed to have been used in the incident.
“The firearm was found hidden at a hut not far from the suspect’s home. It had been placed on the ground and covered with a zinc sheet,” he said in a statement.
Police received a report on August 16 after the teenager was injured by a gunshot while cleaning a water catchment area about 1km from his home, he said.
Liong said police investigations later found that the victim had gone hunting in the forest with his relative when he was accidentally shot by his friend, who had mistaken him for an animal.
“The police are continuing investigations, including tracing witnesses and gathering other information related to the case.
“The public is urged to channel any information related to the case to the police and refrain from making speculations,” he said.
He added that the case was being investigated under Section 307 of the Penal Code and Section 37 of the Arms Act 1960. — The Borneo Post

Title: Kuskop to expedite disbursement of PM’s additional RM1b microcredit pledge, says minister
Article:
SERDANG, Aug 31 — The Ministry of Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives (Kuskop) will expedite the disbursement of an additional RM1 billion in microcredit funds to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement yesterday.
Minister Steven Sim said the increase in allocation brings this year’s total microcredit funding to RM6 billion, up from RM5 billion.
“Among the agencies involved in this additional RM1 billion are Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia (AIM) and Tekun Nasional. We will work to speed up the disbursement of the promised funds,” he said.
He was speaking to reporters after officiating the Kuskop Business Malaysia Hub at the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (MAHA) 2026, Malaysia Agro Exposition Park (Maeps) here today.
Yesterday, Anwar, who is also finance minister, announced the additional RM1 billion in micro financing facilities and said the government had agreed to raise the e-invoice exemption threshold from RM1 million to RM3 million annually.
Anwar said the extra funding was aimed at assisting small businesses grappling with rising costs and to support their expansion.
Elaborating further, Sim said the announcement was certainly welcome news for the MSME sector, particularly small and micro businesses.
“This is because microcredit not only provides financial support, but these microcredit agencies are also generally more accommodating to micro and small businesses in terms of requirements, simplifying processes and so on.
“Including the announcement to raise the e-invoice threshold from RM1 million to RM3 million, this is especially important for MSMEs. Based on data from the Finance Ministry, I see that it will benefit over one million companies in this category,” he said.
He also described the increase in RON95 and diesel quotas as the best “Merdeka gift” for Malaysians, particularly those in the MSME sector who rely heavily on their vehicles to earn a living. — Bernama

Title: Election Commission to reveal proposed new, renamed Sarawak state seats on Sept 1
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 31 — The names and locations of Sarawak’s 17 proposed new State Legislative Assembly (DUN) constituencies will finally be publicly unveiled by the Election Commission (EC) tomorrow (September 1).
The announcement is eagerly anticipated as it will provide greater clarity on the proposed expansion of the Sarawak Legislative Assembly from 82 to 99 seats, following the redelineation exercise undertaken by the EC.
A notice on the new seats will be published in
The Borneo Post
and
Utusan Borneo
tomorrow. Similar notices are also to be displayed at selected locations in each parliamentary constituency in the state.
Apart from the new seats, the EC has proposed renaming several existing seats.
The month-long public display of the list is in accordance with Section 4(b), Part II of the Thirteenth Schedule of the Federal Constitution.
It allows for objections or representations with respect to the EC’s proposed recommendations to be made to the Commission within one month after the date of publication of the notice.
Section 5, Part II of the same legislation states that such representations objecting to the proposed recommendations may be made by the state government, any local authority whose area is wholly or partly comprised in the constituencies affected by the recommendations, or a body of 100 or more persons whose names are shown on the current electoral rolls of the constituencies in question.
The proposed increase of 17 seats was approved by the Sarawak Legislative Assembly on July 7, 2025, when it passed the Dewan Undangan Negeri (Composition of Membership) Bill 2025.
It was reported that the proposed increase was intended to reflect demographic changes, urban expansion, and the growing demand for equitable representation.
The Bill also noted that the last redelineation exercise in Sarawak was carried out in 2015, whereas population and voter numbers had increased significantly since then. The voting age had also been lowered from 21 to 18 since then.
However, the unveiling of the names will not necessarily mean the 17 seats will be contested in the coming 13th state election, which could be held before the end of this year.
The proposed seats would have to be presented to Parliament for approval and then gazetted before they can be implemented.
The last Sarawak state election was held on December 18, 2021. — The Borneo Post

Title: Penang council seizes licensed dog after viral video shows attack on stray in Tanjung Bungah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Penang authorities have seized a licensed dog after a viral video showed it repeatedly attacking a smaller stray in Tanjung Bungah, with the incident now under investigation under the Animal Welfare Act 2015.
According to
The Star
, the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) said it seized the dog today after receiving a complaint through its official WhatsApp channel yesterday over the incident at Pearl Hill.
The attack is believed to have happened a day earlier.
MBPP said checks found that the dog had a valid licence and was registered as a mixed breed. The complaint has since been referred to the Veterinary Services Department (DVS) for investigation.
“MBPP will cooperate with DVS regarding further action in the matter,” the council said in a statement.
Footage of the incident, which circulated widely online, shows the dog repeatedly lunging at and biting a smaller white stray while its owner appears to be holding its leash.
The stray, known locally as Tim, struggles to break free before a woman approaches carrying a long stick and drives the attacking dog away.
A separate video later showed Tim limping, with what appeared to be an injury to its left front leg.
It could not immediately be confirmed whether the injury was caused by the attack.
Tim was subsequently taken to a veterinary clinic for treatment and is understood to be in stable condition, according to
The Star
.
Penang DVS director Dr Saira Banu Mohamed Rejab said the department would investigate the incident under the Animal Welfare Act 2015.
MBPP said it was treating the case seriously and would determine what action to take once the investigation was completed.
“MBPP takes this incident seriously and will take appropriate action based on the findings of the investigation and the relevant laws in force,” it said.

Title: ‘Ultraman’ detained near main stage ahead of Sultan Nazrin’s arrival at Perak National Day celebration, says state police chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — A man dressed as Ultraman was detained near the main stage at Perak’s National Day celebrations today after police said his behaviour appeared suspicious in an area where Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah and other members of the Perak royal family were due to be seated.
According to
Berita Harian
, Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the local man, who is in his 40s, was detained at about 5am after he was seen entering and lingering near the main stage area.
“Although he had not caused any disturbance, the man was detained because his behaviour appeared suspicious. Checks also found that the suspect had a record related to mental illness,” Mohd Alwi was quoted as saying after the celebration.
“He did not cause any disturbance. He only came here to watch this morning’s event, but we found his behaviour suspicious.
“So we took immediate action to detain him temporarily, and he does have a psychiatric history.”
Mohd Alwi said the man would be referred to Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta in Tanjung Rambutan for further assessment.
The Perak-level National Day celebration, held in front of Ipoh Town Hall, was attended by Sultan Nazrin and Raja Permaisuri Perak Tuanku Zara Salim.
Also present were Raja Muda Perak Raja Jaafar Raja Muda Musa, Raja Di Hilir Perak Raja Iskandar Dzulkarnain Idris Shah, Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and members of the state executive council.
The incident comes a year after a similar episode at Perak’s National Day celebration, when a woman was detained after being filmed running towards Sultan Nazrin as he stood at attention during the state anthem.
She was later confirmed to have a psychiatric condition, with authorities saying her mental state had affected her actions at the time.

Title: Malaysia Day 2026: Final prep meeting set for Sept 5 ahead of Kuching celebration, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — A meeting to review the final preparations for the 2026 Malaysia Day celebration in Kuching, Sarawak, will be held on September 5, ahead of the main event at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) on September 16.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the official celebration would take place on the night of September 16, with various side events lined up around BCCK and Plaza Merdeka to enliven the Malaysia Day festivities.
“Various events will be held and have been lined up. For more information, refer to Merdeka360,” he told reporters after the 2026 National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya here today.
Fahmi, who is also chairman of the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) main committee, said he was confident that Malaysians from across the country would attend the event, which would feature an exhibition tracing the history of Malaysia’s formation.
He said the main event at the convention centre was also expected to attract about 5,000 attendees.
Fahmi was previously reported to have said that BCCK had been chosen as the venue for the 2026 Malaysia Day celebration, following a decision made during a recent preparatory meeting with Sarawak Minister for Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah, who is co-chairman of this year’s celebrations. — Bernama

Title: ‘Habis madu, sepah dibuang’: Anthony Loke posts Malay proverb after Ong Kian Ming quits DAP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke today posted a Malay proverb on Facebook shortly after former Bangi MP Ong Kian Ming announced his resignation from the party after 14 years.
“
Habis madu, sepah dibuang
,” Loke wrote in the brief post.
The proverb, which literally refers to discarding the residue after the honey has been used up, is commonly used to describe a situation in which someone is cast aside after they are no longer considered useful.
Loke did not name anyone or provide further context for the post.
The timing nevertheless drew questions from social media users over whether it was related to Ong’s departure from DAP.
Ong announced earlier today that his resignation from DAP would take effect today, bringing to an end his membership of the party since 2012. He did not give a reason for leaving.
In his resignation announcement, Ong said he had no plans to join another political party in the near future and would not contest the 16th general election.
He said, however, that he remained committed to a pledge made in January to help former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin campaign in GE16 if Khairy is given a seat to contest.
Ong served as Serdang MP from 2013 to 2018 and Bangi MP from 2018 to 2022, and was deputy international trade and industry minister from 2018 to 2020.
He was also an appointed member of DAP’s central executive committee from 2019 to 2022 and served on the party’s Selangor state committee from 2018 to 2024.
His resignation came two weeks after DAP delegates voted overwhelmingly for the party’s ministers and deputy ministers to remain in the federal government until the end of the current parliamentary term.
Ong had been a prominent voice in the debate ahead of the August 16 vote, publicly setting out arguments both for DAP remaining in government and for leaving the Cabinet to increase pressure on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim over promised reforms.

Title: Voice behind National Day air show, Major Dinnesh brings fighter jet manoeuvres alive
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — As the roar of fighter jets thundered across the skies above Dataran Putrajaya, the spirited voice of Major Dinnesh Nicolas Rene became the bridge between the aerial spectacle and the thousands of eyes fixed skyward, ensuring every manoeuvre was brought to life with precision and passion.
The role of air show commentator, says Dinnesh, a 34-year-old Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) officer, goes far beyond reading a script into a microphone.
It demands extensive knowledge of the aircraft, pilots, formations and every manoeuvre to be performed.
Dinnesh, who has served in the RMAF since 2015, first ventured into this field after being selected as a commentator at the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA) 2019, before continuing the role during the RMAF’s anniversary.
“That was where my career as an air show commentator with the RMAF began,” said the officer, who now serves in the RMAF Air Defence Control Division, in an interview with Bernama.
For the 2026 National Day parade and march-past, Dinnesh took on the role of air commentator alongside Major Neny Suhaida Ab Suki and Captain Muhammad Iqbal Nasrudin.
He said that while his experience as an air defence officer has given him closer insight into the operational aspects that need to be explained during air show commentary, the task still requires substantial preparation.
According to him, preparations begin with meetings and coordination with ground controllers and pilots to ensure that every detail regarding the display is accurately known.
“We need to know what the aircraft will be doing, how many aircraft are involved, who the pilots are, and the motto of each squadron. We also need to coordinate with other security agencies because we must work closely with everyone involved in the air show,” he said.
For large-scale events such as the National Day celebration, which is also attended by the King and the Prime Minister, he said mastery of protocol is among the key challenges.
Dinnesh added that commentators must be aware of what can and cannot be said, while also ensuring that information is delivered at the right moment.
However, he said the biggest challenge for an air show commentator is preserving the voice, the very asset that carries the information and stirs excitement among the crowd amidst the roar of aircraft overhead.
“Unlike a master of ceremonies, a commentator needs to project a powerful voice, so the risk of losing it is very high. Managing and protecting the voice throughout rehearsals right up to the actual day is one of the most critical challenges,” he said.
To ensure the performance remains energetic and maintains its momentum, Dinnesh follows a simple principle: the commentator must first feel and embody the spirit they wish to convey.
He shared that despite years of watching fighter jets up close, his sense of awe and excitement for air shows remains as strong as ever. — Bernama

Title: Roar of fighter jets dominates Putrajaya skies as RMAF stages National Day air show
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — The roar of fighter jets reverberated across the skies over Putrajaya today as the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) staged a thrilling air display, one of the highlights of the 69th National Day celebration.
Royal Malaysian Air Force chief General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris once again took to the cockpit of a Sukhoi Su-30MKM to lead the display, marking the second consecutive year he has personally led the National Day air show.
Four Su-30MKMs, four F/A-18D Hornets and three BAE Hawk 208 fighter jets thundered across the skies, showcasing the nation’s air capabilities and operational readiness.
The 10-minute display began at 9.30 am and featured specially choreographed formations, including the Kite, Diamond, Delta and Victory Combine formations.
The aerial display was further enlivened by commentary from Major Patrick Dinnesh, Major Neny Suhaida Ab Suki and Captain Muhammad Iqbal Nasrudin, who explained the aircraft manoeuvres and formations to spectators.
Fighter aircraft were followed by the appearance of RMAF transport aircraft, including the C-130H Hercules, A400M Atlas and CN235, highlighting the force’s airlift and logistical support capabilities.
The display also featured EC725 and AW139 helicopters operated by the RMAF, flying in formation with assets from the Malaysian Army, Royal Malaysian Navy, Fire and Rescue Department of Malaysia and Royal Malaysia Police.
Each aircraft flypast drew cheers from the thousands of spectators gathered at Dataran Putrajaya, with many keeping their eyes fixed on the skies throughout the display.
The thunderous engines and precision formations transformed the airspace above the federal administrative centre into a dramatic spectacle, adding to the festive atmosphere of the National Day celebration.
For spectators, the air display was among the most eagerly anticipated moments of the celebration, combining entertainment with a demonstration of the capabilities of Malaysia’s air assets. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak to carry out cloud seeding Sept 3 to 5 as haze worsens, four water plants shut
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Sarawak will carry out cloud seeding from September 3 to 5 as authorities grapple with worsening haze and critically low reservoir levels that have already forced four water treatment plants to stop operating.
According to
Harian Metro
, Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) expected conditions to be suitable for the operation during the three-day window.
He said officials would meet tomorrow to determine how the operation would be carried out, with Sarawak Energy Berhad (SEB) dams to be given priority because of their importance to the state’s electricity supply.
“After that, we will move on to water reservoirs where levels have already fallen very low, followed by other areas in need,” he was quoted as saying after a meeting of the Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee in Kuching today.
Uggah, who chairs the committee, said the Rural Water Supply Department had reported that four water treatment plants had been forced to suspend operations because reservoir levels had fallen too low.
The affected plants are in Simunjan in Samarahan Division, Lingga in Sri Aman, Spaoh in Betong and Lichok in Roban.
He said the four areas would be among those prioritised for cloud seeding if weather conditions allowed.
Uggah cautioned, however, that cloud seeding could not simply be carried out on demand because the operation requires suitable cloud formations.
“If there are no clouds, the conditions are not suitable for cloud seeding. It is not that we do not want to do it, but if an aircraft is sent up without producing any results, it would only be a waste of money and the people would become even angrier,” he said.
Sarawak carried out two cloud-seeding operations in May and June after SEB warned that water levels at its dams had reached worrying levels.
The planned operation comes as the state also contends with severe haze.
Uggah said Air Pollutant Index readings at 10am today showed seven locations in the hazardous category, led by Serian at 475.
Tebedu recorded 402, Lubok Antu 375, Lundu 363, Samarahan 333, Kuching 331 and Sri Aman 331.
Sarikei, Sibu and Mukah were in the very unhealthy range, while another eight locations recorded unhealthy air quality.
Uggah said the disaster management committee was continuing to monitor the haze with the Department of Environment and Sarawak Natural Resources and Environment Board, including smoke from fires in Kalimantan being carried into the state by prevailing winds.
He said Sarawak recorded nine hotspots on both August 29 and 30, while Kalimantan recorded 1,180 hotspots and Sumatra 18 on August 29.
Sarawak recorded 302 hotspots between January and August 30, including 186 in August alone.

Title: Malaysia’s King and Queen mark 69th National Day, send greetings to all citizens
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Malaysia’s King and Queen, Their Majesties Sultan Ibrahim and Raja Zarith Sofiah, extended 69th National Day greetings to all Malaysians.
The royal message was conveyed through a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s official Facebook page today.
Earlier, Their Majesties arrived at the National Day celebration in Putrajaya at 8am and were received by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr. Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, as well as Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, who also serves as chairman of the National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) 2026 Main Committee.
Themed “Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati”, the celebration commenced with a military ceremony, followed by stage performances and a colourful parade that reflected the aspirations of Malaysia Madani as a nation that prioritises the wellbeing of its people and honours diversity.
The parade and march-past involved 10,819 participants across 76 contingents, 22 brass bands, 11 decorated vehicles, 328 land, sea and air assets, and 112 service animals, alongside 22 electric vehicles.
Adding to the vibrancy of the event was a human graphic display on the terraces, featuring 26 distinct formations weaving a rich tapestry of Malaysia’s multicultural identity.
The celebration drew over 80,000 visitors. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak says no emergency unless API breaches 500, Serian readings remain hazardous
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 31 — A state of emergency will only be declared if the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaches 500 or above under the National Haze Action Plan, said Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas.
The Sarawak Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) chairman clarified that there is currently no necessity to declare a state of emergency yet.
He explained that should the API breach the 500 mark, the SDMC would immediately escalate the issue to the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) in Kuala Lumpur to facilitate further action in accordance with Nadma Directive No 1.
“I must clarify that if an emergency is declared, it will strictly be enforced within that specific locality, not for the entire state,” Uggah told reporters during a press conference following an SDMC meeting at Wisma Bapa Malaysia on Monday.
He added that under an emergency declaration, all public and private sector offices in the affected area would be required to shut down, with operations permitted only for essential services.
“We are closely monitoring the situation and hope it does not reach the 500 threshold, even though readings are currently nearing that level,” he said.
As of 12.00pm today, the monitoring station at the Serian District Police Headquarters (IPD Serian) recorded an API reading of 463 — a slight drop from its peak of 476 recorded at 8.00am. Both readings remain within the hazardous level.
Uggah assured that SDMC will continue to closely monitor air quality across the state, particularly in locations registering unhealthy, very unhealthy, and hazardous readings.
“The public is advised to refer to the latest official API readings and health advisories, and to take the necessary precautions based on prevailing conditions,” he said.
For areas where API readings reach 201 and above, Uggah urged residents to wear face masks when venturing outdoors — preferably N95 masks, or at minimum 3-ply face masks if N95 masks are unavailable. — The Borneo Post

Title: ‘Not today’: Gobind keeps politics off the table on National Day as questions turn to Ong Kian Ming’s DAP resignation
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — DAP national chairman Gobind Singh Deo today declined to comment on former Bangi MP Ong Kian Ming’s resignation from the party, saying National Day was not the time for politics.
According to the
New Straits Times
, Gobind said he had yet to read Ong’s statement and deferred any response to another time.
“No, not today. No politics today. I haven’t read anything he said, so let’s leave it for another time,” the digital minister said when approached by the national daily during the National Day celebrations here.
Ong announced earlier today that he was resigning from DAP with immediate effect after 14 years in the party.
The former Bangi and Serdang MP said he intended to continue contributing to public life alongside like-minded individuals and would assist former health minister Khairy Jamaluddin in his campaign for the 16th general election.
Ong also said he did not plan to join another political party or contest in GE16.
He joined DAP in 2012 and served as Serdang MP from 2013 to 2018 before representing Bangi from 2018 to 2022. He was also deputy international trade and industry minister from 2018 to 2020, and previously served on the party’s central executive committee and Selangor state committee.
His departure comes two weeks after DAP delegates overwhelmingly backed keeping the party’s ministers and deputy ministers in the federal government until the end of the current parliamentary term.
Ahead of that vote, Ong had publicly discussed the arguments for both remaining in government and withdrawing from Cabinet as a means of pressing Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for faster reforms.

Title: National Day reflections: Zahid stresses TVET jobs, Fadillah calls for harmony and shared future
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — The meaning of independence must be reflected in people’s lives by ensuring they have access to skills, better employment opportunities and are not left behind in the nation’s development, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
Ahmad Zahid said the struggle today was no longer about achieving independence, but ensuring that its true meaning remained alive in the lives of the people.
“As Deputy Prime Minister, to me, independence today means equipping young people with skills, particularly TVET skills, so that they can secure premium-paying jobs in the future,” he said in a National Day video message posted on Facebook today.
He said independence should also create opportunities for small entrepreneurs to grow and enable every family to improve their lives.
The government, he added, must also be there to protect the people during disasters and help them recover and rebuild their lives.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, said his ministry was entrusted with ensuring that national development did not stop at city boundaries but reached every village and rural and remote area.
“Because ultimately, a nation does not become great merely because of what it builds, but because of who it brings along in its development,” he said.
Reflecting on the nation’s journey since independence, he said a single road could transform a village, electricity could bring hope to a modest home, and a small classroom could nurture great aspirations.
He said independence was not merely a date in the history calendar, but a long journey through which a nation builds confidence, determines its future and upholds the dignity of its people.
Ahmad Zahid said independence also meant developing the halal industry, which not only brought pride to Malaysia but also opened markets and livelihood opportunities for Malaysians on the global stage.
“Malaysia is our home. A home bequeathed to us in peace, and it is our responsibility to hand it over to the next generation in a more prosperous, fairer and more equitable condition,” he said.
Meanwhile, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof urged Malaysians to free themselves from division, hatred, prejudice and extremism that could undermine the nation’s harmony.
In a Facebook post today, he said independence was not merely freedom from colonial rule but required Malaysians to ensure that its spirit remained alive within themselves and in their daily lives.
“We may differ in religion, culture, language, customs and backgrounds. Yet we share one homeland, one future and one hope - a peaceful, prosperous and harmonious Malaysia for all,” he said in conjunction with the 69th National Day today.
Fadillah said that amid economic and technological changes, global competition, social challenges and the rapid flow of information, Malaysians must not lose their identity, values and spirit of togetherness.
He therefore called on Malaysians to continue safeguarding unity, respecting diversity, upholding the Federal Constitution and the law, and embracing the principles of the Rukun Negara.
Fadillah said the Malaysia Madani spirit called for a nation that was not only advanced in development but also ensured that prosperity and well-being were enjoyed by all sections of society.
“Independence is not only about what we have inherited, but also about what we will leave behind.
“We want to leave future generations a Malaysia that is just, prosperous, peaceful, united and harmonious,” he said.
Fadillah also urged Malaysians to give meaning to independence through their actions by safeguarding unity, respecting differences, preserving harmony, rejecting hatred and carrying out their responsibilities as citizens with integrity.
This year’s National Day celebration is themed “Malaysia Madani: Well-being for All”. — Bernama

Title: ‘Great show!’ Anwar thanks Malaysians, mingles with crowds at National Day parade
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim praised and expressed his appreciation to everyone involved, as well as members of the public who attended the 2026 National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya here today.
“Great, great show! Alhamdulillah, good. Thank you very much,” he told reporters after watching the 69th National Day parade and procession.
After the colourful, patriotic celebration, Anwar spent time mingling with the enthusiastic crowds, walking more than 500 metres around Dataran Putrajaya and even obliging requests for photographs.
One member of the crowd even thanked the Prime Minister for restoring the monthly basic eligibility quota under the Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) programme from 200 litres to 300 litres, which he announced during the National Day Prime Minister’s Address yesterday.
“Thank you, Datuk Seri, for increasing Budi95,” the man said.
The celebration, which began at 8am, was graced by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim and Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, the King and Queen of Malaysia. Their Majesties were received on arrival by Anwar and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, as well as Communications Minister and 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) Main Committee chairman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
Themed “Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati”, the celebration began with a military ceremony, followed by stage performances and a colourful parade showcasing the Malaysia Madani vision of a nation that prioritises the people’s well-being and respects diversity.
The parade involved 10,819 participants across 76 contingents and 22 marching bands, as well as 11 decorated vehicles, 328 land, sea and air assets, 112 service animals and 22 electric vehicles (EVs). It also featured a human graphics performance on the terraces.
More than 100,000 people joined the celebration, with some camping at Dataran Putrajaya since yesterday evening, while others began arriving in large numbers early this morning.
Yesterday, Anwar announced six key government initiatives for the people’s well-being in his National Day Address, including restoring the Budi95 monthly quota to 300 litres, benefiting more than 16 million users of subsidised RON95.
He also said more than half a million eligible owners of diesel-powered pickup trucks and jeeps would receive up to 400 litres of Budi Diesel monthly, effective Sept 1. — Bernama

Title: Putrajaya’s free water taxis become crowd favourite, offering scenic shortcut to National Day venue
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — The free water taxi service emerged as a highlight for visitors at the 2026 National Day celebration in Dataran Putrajaya today, with people from all walks of life seizing the opportunity to cross Putrajaya Lake in a spirit of patriotism.
Operating from 5 am until noon, the service drew visitors heading to the parade venue and quickly became one of the standout attractions of the celebration.
The journey across Putrajaya Lake also offered people a chance to enjoy the surrounding views of the Federal administrative centre from a different perspective, making it one of the more memorable highlights of this year’s National Day celebration.
Michelle Wong, 31, said she and two other family members made a last-minute decision to attend the celebration here, with a quick Internet search for public transport information.
“We managed to park at the Terra 8 area and took the water taxi here. This is our first time at Dataran Putrajaya and our first time experiencing the water taxi.
“We were given safety jackets, and we really enjoyed the early morning scenery in Putrajaya,” said the digital marketing professional.
Teacher Hajar Salih, 27, who also used the water taxi service, said this was her second time using the service, having enjoyed a similar experience last year.
“I find this the most convenient option for me because I arrived early at the Marina Jetty area and didn’t have to wait long for a water taxi,” said the Gombak resident.
A Bernama check revealed that the water taxi service operated on three routes, with three water taxis available on Route 1 and Route 2, while three cruiser units were provided on Route 3.
Safety was also given due attention, with visitors required to wear life jackets throughout the journey.
Route 1 runs from the Terra 8 Jetty, Presint 8, to the Monument Jetty, Presint 2, while Route 2 connects the Putrajaya Lake Club Jetty to the Monument Jetty, Presint 2.
Route 3 operates between the Putrajaya Marina Jetty, Presint 5, and the Anjung Floria Jetty, Presint 4.
In addition to the water taxi service, the public could also take advantage of free shuttle bus services for the celebration.
The free shuttle bus service on Route MS01 from Putrajaya Sentral Terminal to Jalan Tun Abdul Razak, Presint 2, operates non-stop for 24 hours, starting from 2 pm yesterday to 2 pm today.
Another free shuttle bus service, Route MS02, operates from the main lobby of PICC, Jalan P4X, Presint 4, from 4 am to 2 pm today, with buses every five minutes. — Bernama

Title: Upin & Ipin, police dogs and fighter jets steal the show at Malaysia’s 69th National Day parade
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 31 — Tens of thousands of Malaysians packed Dataran Putrajaya for the National Day parade today, many with Jalur Gemilang motifs painted on their cheeks and national flags in hand.
Some families appeared to have camped overnight to secure the best vantage points for the annual parade, while those unable to get a front-row view followed the livestreams on their phones as they waited patiently behind a sea of spectators.
His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, attend National Day 2026 celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya in Putrajaya on August 31, 2026. — Bernama pic
The ceremony began at 8am with the arrival of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, who were escorted to the stage by royal guards and members of the Malaysian Armed Forces.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datin Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, were also present.
A giant Jalur Gemilang is carried past His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, during the National Day 2026 celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya in Putrajaya August 31, 2026. — Bernama pic
The Royal Artillery Regiment fired a 14-gun salute representing the states and Federal Territories as the crowd sang the national anthem.
Participants wear traditional attire during the National Day 2026 parade at Dataran Putrajaya in Putrajaya on August 31, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Dozens of colourful floats from ministries and agencies then made their way through the square, including the eagerly awaited Fire and Rescue Department contingent, where several firemen drew cheers by flexing their well-toned muscles.
A marching contingent is seen during the National Day 2026 parade at Dataran Putrajaya in Putrajaya on August 31, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Even members of the Carsome Malaysia contingent got in on the act, mimicking the firemen’s poses in an attempt to catch the crowd’s attention.
People attend National Day 2026 celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya in Putrajaya on August 31, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Another crowd favourite was the Upin & Ipin float by the Communications Ministry, which sent young children into cheers at the sight of the beloved cartoon characters.
The Upin & Ipin float by the Communications Ministry is seen during the National Day 2026 parade at Dataran Putrajaya in Putrajaya on August 31, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Also braving the heat were canines from the Royal Malaysia Police K9 unit, with thousands cheering and waving as the dogs marched calmly alongside their handlers.
A column of tanks is seen during the National Day 2026 parade at Dataran Putrajaya in Putrajaya on August 31, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Just before the parade drew to a close, the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) staged a spectacular flypast, prompting another roar from the crowds gathered below.
Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) fighter jets soar above the crowd during the National Day 2026 parade at Dataran Putrajaya in Putrajaya on August 31, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Fighter jets streaked across the sky and released decoy flares during the aerial display, sending thousands of spectators reaching for their phones to capture the moment.
A Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) fighter jet participates in an aerial display during the National Day 2026 parade at Dataran Putrajaya in Putrajaya on August 31, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa
The aircraft had departed from Subang Air Base earlier in the day, led by RMAF chief General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris, who piloted a Sukhoi Su-30MKM.
A vibrant showcase of captivating performances and creative displays enlivens the National Day 2026 parade at Dataran Putrajaya in Putrajaya on August 31, 2026. — Bernama pic

Title: ‘Harsh, but true’: Kedah MB stands by gambling remarks, denies targeting Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 31 — Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor has stood by his controversial remarks over gambling, saying that although his words were harsh, they were directed at gambling interests and not Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
According to the
New Straits Times
, Sanusi said he was reiterating the point to prevent the public from being misled by interpretations of what he had said.
“I targeted the gambling tycoons. I did not target ustaz, religious leaders or the prime minister. I targeted the gambling tycoons.
“Have the courage to speak the truth.
“They are harsh words, but they are true,” he said while speaking at the Generasi Pewaris Sejahtera Negeri Kedah 2026 convention in Alor Setar yesterday.
Sanusi said the issue had continued to attract comments “day and night” and urged the public to refer to the “original source” rather than rely on interpretations by others.
He said he would continue to use his position as menteri besar to speak out and take action where he had the authority to do so.
“I have the authority to act, so I take action at my level. I have the space to speak, so I speak,” he said.
Sanusi has faced criticism over earlier remarks that some interpreted as wishing ill on Anwar in connection with the gambling issue.
He has denied that interpretation, maintaining that his comments were aimed instead at those who had sponsored legal action seeking to overturn the Kedah government’s ban on lottery operations in the state.
The dispute dates back to November 2021, when Sanusi announced that the Kedah government would stop issuing and renewing premises licences for lottery and number-betting outlets. Physical lottery outlets have consequently been unable to operate in the state since 2023 despite holding federal licences.
Lottery operators challenged the policy in court, and the High Court ruled in 2024 that the state government’s decision was unlawful and unconstitutional. That decision was upheld by the Court of Appeal in December 2025, which found that Kedah could not use its powers over premises licensing to impose a blanket prohibition on an activity regulated at the federal level.
On August 12, the Federal Court rejected Kedah’s application for leave to appeal, effectively ending the state government’s legal bid to defend the ban.

Title: Twenty‑three injured after tour bus crashes at Kanowit roundabout along Pan Borneo Highway
Article:
SIBU, Aug 31 — Twenty-three people were injured after a tour bus was involved in a single-vehicle accident at the Kanowit roundabout along the Pan Borneo Highway here early Monday.
A statement from the Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) operations centre said it received a distress call at 2.25am and deployed six firefighters from the Sibu Jaya fire station to the scene.
“A total of 43 people were in the bus when the accident occurred. Twenty-three of them sustained injuries, of whom 19 were women and four were men.
“No victims were trapped in the bus.
“Firefighters assisted one female victim who was still inside the bus to a safe location, while the other 42 victims had been assisted out by members of the public before the arrival of the firefighters,” the statement said.
It said the injured victims received initial treatment from medical personnel before being taken to Sibu Hospital and Kanowit Hospital for further treatment.
The operation ended at 4.50am after firefighters ensured the scene was safe and no further action was required.
The operation also involved the police, Health Ministry and Civil Defence Force. — The Borneo Post
